7. [Couche 2 : Registre fédéré de miroirs (cross-repo)](#7-couche-2-registre-fédéré-de-miroirs-cross-repo)
8. [Couche 3 : Gestion d'erreurs et actions contextuelles](#8-couche-3-gestion-derreurs-et-actions-contextuelles)
9. [Spécifications par écosystème](#9-spécifications-par-écosystème)
10. [Considérations de sécurité et de confidentialité](#10-considérations-de-sécurité-et-de-confidentialité)
11. [Plan d'implémentation proposé](#11-plan-dimplémentation-proposé)
12. [Limites déclarées](#12-limites-déclarées)
13. [Conclusion](#13-conclusion)

---

## 1. Contexte et diagnostic de l'écosystème (juillet 2026)

L'écosystème des extensions pour applications d'anime, manga et light novels a connu des transformations majeures entre 2024 et 2026. La discontinuation d'Aniyomi en avril 2026, les pressions légales sur Kotatsu et la fragmentation des dépôts ont créé un paysage technique complexe où la résilience des extensions est devenue un enjeu critique.

### 1.1. Constats principaux

- **Changements de domaine massifs** : des sites comme HiAnime (ex-Aniwatch/Zoro.to) ont fermé en mars 2026 suite à une désignation USTR. Les sites de streaming non officiels changent de domaine fréquemment, rendant les extensions inopérantes jusqu'à une mise à jour manuelle du code source.
- **Dépôts isolés** : chaque mainteneur gère ses propres extensions ; il n'existe pas de mécanisme pour partager des informations sur les domaines alternatifs entre dépôts. Si Hollow (FR) détecte un nouveau domaine pour Anime-Sama, Keiyoushi ou Secozzi ne peuvent pas en bénéficier automatiquement.
- **Absence d'auto-réparation dans les applications hôtes** : Mihon v0.20.1, Dantotsu v3.2.2 et LNReader v2.0.3 ne disposent pas de détection automatique des domaines morts ni de changement d'URL à chaud. Les utilisateurs doivent attendre une mise à jour de l'APK ou chercher manuellement un nouveau dépôt.

---

## 2. État des applications hôtes

| Application | État | Format d'extension | Observation |
|-------------|------|---------------------|-------------|
| **Mihon** | Actif (v0.20.1) | APK + `index.min.json` | Successeur principal de Tachiyomi. Supporte `tachiyomix` 1.6. Terminologie : "extension store" au lieu de "extension repo". |
| **Dantotsu** | Actif (v3.2.2+) | APK + `index.min.json` | Fork inspiré de Saikou. Compatible avec les extensions Tachi/Aniyomi. |
| **ReDantotsu** | Actif | APK + `index.min.json` | Remake avec nouvelles fonctionnalités (MAL sync, Liquid Glass). |
| **LNReader** | Actif (v2.0.3) | Plugins JS + `.dist/plugins.min.json` | Écosystème séparé basé sur Node.js. 260 plugins, 16 langues. |
| **Aniyomi** | Discontinué (avril 2026) | APK + `index.min.json` | Plus de développement actif. Transition vers un modèle "bring-your-own-content". |
| **Kotatsu** | En déclin | Propre | Problèmes légaux (Kakao). Non recommandé comme base. |
| **Mangayomi** | Actif | APK bridge | Cross-platform. Nécessite `apkbridge` pour les extensions Mihon/Aniyomi. |

**Donnée vérifiée :** Aniyomi a cessé son développement actif en avril 2026. Les utilisateurs ont migré massivement vers Dantotsu et Mihon. Toute nouvelle proposition doit cibler Mihon/Dantotsu comme base primaire, avec LNReader comme écosystème parallèle pour les light novels.

---

## 3. Dépôts actifs identifiés

| Dépôt | Plateforme | Contenu | URL de l'index |
|-------|------------|---------|----------------|
| **Keiyoushi** | GitHub | Manga (Mihon) | `raw.githubusercontent.com/keiyoushi/extensions/repo/index.min.json` |
| **Secozzi** | GitHub | Anime (Aniyomi/Dantotsu) | `raw.githubusercontent.com/Secozzi/aniyomi-extensions/refs/heads/repo/index.min.json` |
| **Hollow (FR)** | Codeberg | Anime FR (Aniyomi/Dantotsu) | `codeberg.org/hollow/aniyomi-extensions-fr/media/branch/repo/index.min.json` |
| **Yūzōnō** | GitHub | Anime | `raw.githubusercontent.com/yuzono/anime-repo/repo/index.min.json` |
| **Kohi-den** | GitHub | Anime/Manga | `kohiden.xyz/Kohi-den/extensions/raw/branch/main/index.min.json` |
| **LNReader Official** | GitHub | Light novels | `raw.githubusercontent.com/LNReader/lnreader-plugins/plugins/v3.0.0/.dist/plugins.min.json` |

**Donnée vérifiée :** Le dépôt `bluecxt/anime-extensions-french` (objet du issue #40 original) n'apparaît plus dans les listes actives de wotaku.wiki ni miyomi.app. L'écosystème français de l'anime est désormais principalement représenté par Hollow sur Codeberg, qui regroupe 10 extensions : AniZone, Sudatchi, Anime-Sama, AniSama, FrAnime, French Anime, HDS, JetAnime, Vostfree et Wiflix.

---

## 4. Problème central : fragmentation et fragilité

L'écosystème actuel présente trois vulnérabilités structurelles :

1. **Changements de domaine massifs** : les sites de streaming non officiels changent de domaine avec une fréquence élevée. Lorsque cela se produit, les extensions restent inopérantes jusqu'à ce qu'un mainteneur mette à jour le code source et reconstruise l'APK.
2. **Dépôts isolés** : chaque mainteneur gère ses propres extensions. Il n'existe pas de mécanisme pour que les dépôts partagent des informations sur les domaines alternatifs. Si Hollow (FR) détecte un nouveau domaine pour Anime-Sama, Keiyoushi ou Secozzi ne peuvent pas bénéficier de cette information.
3. **Absence d'auto-réparation dans l'application hôte** : Mihon v0.20.1 n'inclut pas de détection automatique des domaines morts ni de changement d'URL en temps réel. L'utilisateur doit attendre une mise à jour de l'APK ou rechercher manuellement un nouveau dépôt.

---

## 5. Proposition : un standard de résilience fédéré

Au lieu d'une solution monolithique pour un seul dépôt, nous proposons un standard cross-écosystème que tout dépôt et toute application compatible peuvent adopter. L'objectif est qu'une extension puisse se remettre d'un changement de domaine sans nécessiter une nouvelle compilation de l'APK.

Le standard se compose de trois couches :

---

## 6. Couche 1 : Préférences d'URL par extension (niveau APK)

### 6.1. Contexte technique actuel

Dans l'écosystème Mihon/Dantotsu, les extensions sont des APK qui implémentent des interfaces telles que `Source` ou `HttpSource`. L'URL de base est généralement codée en dur comme une propriété `override val baseUrl`. Mihon v0.20.1 a introduit le support de `tachiyomix` 1.6, qui étend les capacités du format d'extension.

### 6.2. Proposition : interface `ResilientSource`

Définir une interface optionnelle que les extensions peuvent implémenter pour exposer la configurabilité de l'URL à l'utilisateur :

```kotlin
/**
 * Interface optionnelle pour les extensions permettant de modifier l'URL de base.
 * Compatible avec Mihon 0.20.x, Dantotsu 3.2.x et les forks dérivés.
 */
interface ResilientSource {
    /** URL par défaut, immuable, définie par le mainteneur */
    val defaultBaseUrl: String

    /** URL actuellement utilisée (peut être personnalisée) */
    var currentBaseUrl: String

    /** Liste des miroirs connus pour cette source */
    fun getKnownMirrors(): List<MirrorEntry>

    /** Vérifie si une URL répond correctement */
    suspend fun probeUrl(url: String): ProbeResult

    /** Restaure l'URL par défaut */
    fun resetToDefault()
}

data class MirrorEntry(
    val url: String,
    val region: String?,
    val reliabilityScore: Int,        // 0-100, basé sur le succès des connexions
    val lastVerified: Long?,          // timestamp
    val verifiedBy: String?,          // dépôt ou communauté ayant vérifié
    val notes: String?
)

sealed class ProbeResult {
    data class Success(val latencyMs: Long) : ProbeResult()
    data class Failure(val reason: FailureReason) : ProbeResult()
}

enum class FailureReason {
    DNS_UNRESOLVED, HTTP_ERROR, SSL_ERROR, TIMEOUT, UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE
}
```

6.3. Persistance

Les préférences sont stockées dans le SharedPreferences standard de l'extension (mécanisme déjà existant dans Mihon/Dantotsu pour les configurations de source). Aucune modification de la base de données de l'application hôte n'est requise.

6.4. UX dans l'application hôte

Lorsqu'une extension implémente ResilientSource, l'écran de configuration de la source affiche :

· Champ de texte modifiable avec l'URL actuelle
· Bouton "Tester la connexion" qui exécute probeUrl()
· Liste déroulante des miroirs connus (triés par reliabilityScore)
· Bouton "Restaurer les valeurs par défaut"
· Indicateur visuel de l'état de la dernière connexion

---

7. Couche 2 : Registre fédéré de miroirs (cross-repo)

7.1. Le problème de la fragmentation

Actuellement, si Anime-Sama change de domaine :

· Hollow (FR) met à jour son code source et reconstruit l'APK
· Les utilisateurs doivent attendre que GitHub Actions génère le nouvel APK
· Les autres dépôts (Secozzi, Yūzōnō, Kohi-den) ne sont pas informés du changement
· Les utilisateurs de Dantotsu utilisant Anime-Sama restent sans service jusqu'à la mise à jour

7.2. Solution : mirrors.json fédéré

Créer un fichier standard mirrors.json que tout dépôt peut héberger et consommer. La fédération permet aux dépôts de se synchroniser entre eux.

7.2.1. Structure du fichier

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "1.0",
  "lastUpdated": 1751234567890,
  "upstream": [
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/keiyoushi/extensions/repo/mirrors.json",
    "https://codeberg.org/hollow/aniyomi-extensions-fr/media/branch/repo/mirrors.json"
  ],
  "mirrors": [
    {
      "extensionPkg": "eu.kanade.tachiyomi.animeextension.fr.animesama",
      "extensionName": "Anime-Sama",
      "defaultUrl": "https://anime-sama.fr",
      "entries": [
        {
          "url": "https://anime-sama.me",
          "region": "FR",
          "reliabilityScore": 95,
          "lastVerified": 1751234567890,
          "verifiedBy": "hollow@codeberg",
          "verificationMethod": "manual",
          "notes": "Domaine alternatif confirmé par la communauté"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

7.2.2. Mécanisme de fédération

Chaque dépôt publie son mirrors.json dans la branche repo (à côté de index.min.json). Les dépôts déclarent upstream pour indiquer de qui ils consomment des données. Le système résout les conflits par horodatage (lastVerified le plus récent l'emporte).

7.2.3. Vérification et sécurité

Niveau Méthode Description
0 Non vérifié Soumis par un utilisateur via PR
1 Vérification automatique CI exécute probeUrl() et confirme HTTP 200 + structure attendue
2 Vérification manuelle Un mainteneur du dépôt confirme le domaine
3 Cross-repo Le miroir apparaît dans au moins 2 dépôts indépendants avec reliabilityScore > 80

Restriction de sécurité : Seules les URLs avec le schéma https:// sont acceptées. Les domaines avec certificats auto-signés ou sur des listes de réputation douteuse sont automatiquement rejetés.

7.2.4. Intégration dans le build des extensions

Pendant le processus CI (GitHub Actions ou Codeberg CI), le système de build peut :

1. Lire mirrors.json du dépôt
2. Injecter les miroirs connus en tant que ressource brute dans l'APK (res/raw/known_mirrors.json)
3. Permettre à l'extension d'avoir des miroirs préchargés sans dépendre de la connectivité lors du premier usage

---

8. Couche 3 : Gestion d'erreurs et actions contextuelles

8.1. Le problème actuel

Lorsqu'une extension échoue, Mihon/Dantotsu affiche des erreurs génériques comme "HTTP 404" ou "Failed to connect". L'utilisateur ne distingue pas entre :

· Domaine tombé
· Rate limiting du serveur
· Changement de structure HTML (nécessite une mise à jour du scraper)
· Problème de réseau local

8.2. Proposition : exceptions sémantiques avec actions associées

Étendre le modèle d'erreur actuel avec des exceptions que l'application hôte peut traduire en actions UI :

```kotlin
sealed class SourceException(
    message: String,
    cause: Throwable? = null
) : Exception(message, cause)

class DomainChangedException(
    message: String,
    val suggestedMirrors: List<MirrorEntry>
) : SourceException(message)

class RateLimitException(
    message: String,
    val retryAfterSeconds: Int?
) : SourceException(message)

class ScraperBrokenException(
    message: String
) : SourceException(message)

class SourceUnavailableException(
    message: String
) : SourceException(message)
```

8.3. Flux de récupération automatique

Lorsqu'une extension lève DomainChangedException :

1. L'application hôte affiche une boîte de dialogue : "Le domaine de [Source] semble avoir changé. X miroirs alternatifs ont été trouvés."
2. L'utilisateur sélectionne un miroir ou en saisit un manuellement
3. L'application exécute probeUrl() en arrière-plan
4. En cas de succès, elle met à jour currentBaseUrl via ResilientSource
5. Elle réessaie l'opération originale automatiquement
6. Optionnellement, elle demande à l'utilisateur s'il souhaite signaler le miroir fonctionnel au dépôt (pour alimenter la base fédérée)

8.4. Différenciation des causes

Symptôme Diagnostic probable Action suggérée
HTTP 404 sur l'URL racine Domaine changé Rechercher des miroirs
HTTP 200 mais HTML inattendu Scraper obsolète Notifier le mainteneur du dépôt
HTTP 429 Rate limiting Attendre et réessayer
Échec SSL handshake Blocage régional ou certificat invalide Suggérer VPN ou miroir alternatif
Timeout persistant Source tombée temporairement Réessayer avec backoff exponentiel

---

9. Spécifications par écosystème

9.1. Mihon / Dantotsu / ReDantotsu (format APK)

Format de dépôt : index.min.json avec métadonnées des extensions APK.

Adaptation proposée :

· Les extensions nouvelles ou mises à jour implémentent ResilientSource de manière optionnelle
· Le index.min.json peut inclure un champ optionnel mirrorsUrl pointant vers le mirrors.json fédéré du dépôt
· L'application hôte (Mihon/Dantotsu) peut consulter mirrorsUrl lorsqu'elle détecte des erreurs récurrentes d'une extension

Compatibilité ascendante : Les extensions qui n'implémentent pas ResilientSource fonctionnent exactement comme avant. Le standard est opt-in.

9.2. LNReader (format Plugin JS)

Format de dépôt : .dist/plugins.min.json avec plugins écrits en JavaScript/TypeScript.

Adaptation proposée :

· Chaque plugin expose une fonction optionnelle getResilientConfig() qui retourne :

```typescript
interface ResilientConfig {
  defaultUrl: string;
  knownMirrors: MirrorEntry[];
  probeUrl: (url: string) => Promise<ProbeResult>;
}
```

· Le dépôt de LNReader peut héberger un mirrors.json fédéré à la racine de la branche plugins
· L'hôte (LNReader v2.0.3+) consulte ce fichier lorsqu'un plugin échoue de manière persistante



### Other details

9.3. Dépôts identifiés pour une adoption pilote

Dépôt Priorité Justification
Hollow (FR) sur Codeberg Élevée Successeur naturel de l'écosystème français. 10 extensions actives, sur Codeberg (moins d'exposition DMCA que GitHub)
Secozzi (GitHub) Élevée Dépôt d'anime le plus stable post-Aniyomi. Peut servir de pont entre écosystèmes
Keiyoushi (GitHub) Moyenne Plus grand dépôt de manga. L'adoption ici validerait le standard à grande échelle
LNReader Official Moyenne Écosystème séparé mais avec des besoins similaires

---

10. Considérations de sécurité et de confidentialité

1. Vérification des miroirs : Tout domaine suggéré doit passer par une vérification automatique (CI) avant d'apparaître dans mirrors.json. Les mainteneurs doivent examiner manuellement les changements de domaine des sources populaires.
2. HTTPS obligatoire : Le standard rejette les URLs avec http://. Cela protège contre l'interception de credentials sur les sites nécessitant une connexion.
3. Données locales : Les URLs personnalisées par l'utilisateur ne sont jamais transmises à des serveurs centraux. Elles sont stockées uniquement dans SharedPreferences locales.
4. Anti-phishing : Le système peut comparer les domaines suggérés avec des listes publiques de réputation (Google Safe Browsing, PhishTank) avant de les présenter à l'utilisateur.
5. Avertissement sur les dépôts non officiels : Comme l'a souligné l'équipe d'Aniyomi lors de sa discontinuation, les dépôts tiers peuvent contenir des malwares. Le standard doit inclure un mécanisme de signature ou de checksum pour les fichiers mirrors.json.

---

11. Plan d'implémentation proposé

Phase Livrable Dépendances Complexité estimée
1 Spécification formelle du standard ResilientSource et mirrors.json Consensus des mainteneurs de Hollow, Secozzi et Keiyoushi Faible
2 Implémentation de référence dans 2 extensions de Hollow (FR) Finalisation de la spécification Moyenne
3 Script CI pour la vérification automatique des miroirs Dépôt avec GitHub Actions ou Codeberg CI Moyenne
4 PR à Mihon/Dantotsu pour le support UI de ResilientSource Acceptation par les mainteneurs de l'application hôte Élevée
5 Extension du standard aux plugins LNReader Coordination avec l'équipe de LNReader Moyenne
6 Documentation et guide pour les mainteneurs de dépôts Phases 1-3 terminées Faible

---

12. Limites déclarées

· Les interfaces proposées (ResilientSource, mirrors.json) sont conceptuelles et n'ont pas été implémentées ni testées dans une application réelle.
· L'adoption du standard dépend de la volonté des mainteneurs de dépôts indépendants ; aucune autorité centrale ne peut l'imposer.
· Les changements de domaine ne résolvent pas tous les cas d'extension cassée : si un site change sa structure HTML/JSON, le scraper nécessite toujours une mise à jour manuelle.
· La vérification des dépôts et des miroirs proposés est partielle ; une validation manuelle par les mainteneurs reste nécessaire.
· Les données sur l'état des applications et dépôts sont basées sur des sources publiques consultées en juillet 2026 et peuvent évoluer.

---

13. Conclusion

L'écosystème des extensions d'anime, manga et light novels en 2026 est plus fragmenté qu'en 2024, mais aussi plus diversifié. Aniyomi n'est plus la base commune ; Mihon, Dantotsu et LNReader ont pris des rôles distincts. Une proposition de résilience qui ne ciblerait qu'un seul dépôt ou une seule application deviendrait rapidement obsolète.

La clé réside dans un standard fédéré : que chaque dépôt maintienne son autonomie, mais partage des informations sur les miroirs via un format commun. Cela réduit la charge sur les mainteneurs individuels et permet aux utilisateurs de récupérer leurs extensions sans attendre des cycles de compilation.

La proposition originale en trois couches reste conceptuellement solide. Ce qui change, c'est le contexte : il ne s'agit plus d'un seul dépôt français pour Aniyomi, mais d'un réseau de dépôts cross-plateforme qui peut bénéficier à des milliers d'utilisateurs sur plusieurs applications.

---

Vérification et limites

· Date de vérification : 28 juillet 2026.
· Non vérifiable extérieurement : l'état exact du code source des applications hôtes, les décisions internes des mainteneurs, les métriques d'utilisation des dépôts.
· Écarts possibles : Les interfaces et structures proposées peuvent nécessiter des ajustements pour être compatibles avec les implémentations réelles de Mihon v0.20.1, Dantotsu v3.2.2 et LNReader v2.0.3.
· Sources des données de l'écosystème : wotaku.wiki, miyomi.app, changelogs de Mihon, dépôts actifs de Keiyoushi, Secozzi, Hollow (Codeberg) et LNReader. Les affirmations sur les fonctionnalités sont basées sur la documentation publique et les journaux de modifications ; les détails d'implémentation n'ont pas été vérifiés par examen du code source.

---

☑ Cette proposition n'est pas un doublon d'un problème existant. Veuillez consulter la liste des problèmes ouverts avant d'en créer un nouveau.

titulo: 🌊🐋 SUGGESTION FOR TONKATSU BOX: AI-POWERED AUTOMATIC TRANSLATION FOR METADATA AND CONTENT
body_original:
A proposal to take Tonkatsu Box's language accessibility to the next level, allowing every user to enjoy their collection in their own language. 🤖🌍📚



🎯 THE PROBLEM: METADATA IN FOREIGN LANGUAGES

Tonkatsu Box is an exceptional application for organizing collections of games, movies, anime, manga, and books. It allows searching millions of titles from sources such as IGDB, TMDB, AniList, MangaBaka, VNDB, and Google Books. However, the metadata it retrieves from these sources — titles, descriptions, synopses, reviews, genres — is in the original languages in which they were created.

This creates a significant barrier for:

· Users who do not master English, Russian, or Chinese (the only interface languages).
· Collectors who want to read detailed descriptions in their native tongue.
· People discovering new content who need to understand what it's about before adding it to their collection.

The solution: Implement an AI-powered automatic translation system that translates all metadata into the user's selected language.

---

💡 THE PROPOSED SOLUTION

🧠 1. AI-Powered Automatic Metadata Translation

Tonkatsu Box could integrate an automatic translation system that, upon retrieving metadata from external sources (IGDB, TMDB, AniList, etc.), translates it into the user's preferred language.

How it would work:

1. The user selects their preferred language in Settings → App Language.
2. When the application retrieves metadata from an external source, it sends the text (title, description, synopsis, etc.) to a translation service.
3. The translated text is stored in Tonkatsu Box's local database.
4. The user sees all content in their language, with no extra effort.

Implementation options:

Option Description Advantages Disadvantages
External translation API Use Google Translate API, DeepL API, or Microsoft Translator High quality, support for many languages Cost per use, requires API key
Local AI model Integrate a lightweight translation model (e.g., Meta's NLLB-200) Free, private, no internet dependency Higher resource consumption, variable quality
Hybrid translation Use API for major languages, local model for fallback Balance between quality and cost Implementation complexity

💡 The Little Whale's recommendation: Start with an external translation API (optional, user-provided key) and, in the long term, explore integrating a local AI model for users who prefer privacy and offline functionality.

🔄 2. Translating the User Interface to More Languages

Currently, Tonkatsu Box only has its interface in English, Russian, and Simplified Chinese. The proposal includes:

· Adding Spanish as a native interface language.
· Allowing the community to contribute translations to other languages through a collaborative system (e.g., Weblate, Crowdin).
· Using AI to assist in translating interface strings, reducing manual work.

🌍 3. Automatic Language Detection of Content

AI could automatically detect the source language of metadata and offer translation only when necessary, avoiding unnecessary translations.

🏷️ 4. Translation of Tags and Categories

Tags, genres, and categories could also be translated, allowing for more intuitive navigation in the user's language.

---

🔧 SUGGESTED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

Phase Task Description
1 API Evaluation Research and select the most suitable translation API (Google Translate, DeepL, etc.)
2 Basic Integration Add support for translating titles and descriptions when retrieving metadata
3 Local Storage Store translations in the local database to avoid repeated API calls
4 Language Configuration Add options in Settings to choose the language of translated metadata
5 Interface Translation Add Spanish and other languages to the UI through a collaborative system
6 Optimization Implement translation caching and automatic language detection
7 Local Model (optional) Explore integrating a lightweight AI model for offline translation

---

✅ EXPECTED BENEFITS

Benefit Description
Accessibility Users from all over the world can enjoy Tonkatsu Box in their native language
Discovery Reading descriptions in your language makes discovering new content easier
Community Attracts more Spanish-speaking and other regional users
Competitiveness Differentiates Tonkatsu Box from similar applications
Privacy The option for local translation protects user data

---

🔗 REFERENCES FROM SIMILAR APPLICATIONS

Kototoro: Local Translation + OCR

Kototoro already implements an OCR + local translation system directly within its reader. Users can download translation models and use them offline. This approach demonstrates that automatic translation in content management applications is viable and valued by users.

Komi Store: Multilingual Localization

Komi Store (now Komi Store) has implemented a localization system that allows users to change the interface language and see application descriptions in their native language. Although it doesn't use AI for automatic translations, its focus on language accessibility is a model to follow.

---

**Warning:** Internal source code, exact architecture (BLoC/Riverpod/etc.), and database schema have not been verified. Implementation suggestions are inferences based on common Flutter patterns and the visible interface.

---

## 2. VERIFIED DATA — Consulted Wikis and Resources

| **EverythingMoe.com** | Curated toplist of streaming, manga, novels, games, apps, downloads, music, calendars, trackers | Medium: broad ecosystem overview; useful for identifying APIs and metadata sources |
| **FMHY.net/video** | Massive index of streaming, downloads, torrents, trackers, subtitles, video tools | Low-Medium for direct features; High for understanding the media consumption ecosystem |
| **FMHY.net/gaming** | Index of game downloads, ROMs, emulators, abandonware, decompilations, remakes, browser games | Medium: reference for retro gaming and emulation tracking features |
| **FMHY.net/reading** | Index of ebooks, comics, manga, light novels, fanfiction, audiobooks, magazines, academic papers | Medium-High: reference for metadata sources for books, comics, and manga |

**Important Limitation:** FMHY, Wotaku, and EverythingMoe resources contain indices that include both legal and legally ambiguous resources. This analysis explicitly filters only suggestions applicable to a legitimate open-source personal collection management project. Integration with unauthorized content distribution sources is not suggested.

---

## 3. COMPATIBILITY ANALYSIS — Tonkatsu Box Philosophy

**Inferred philosophy of the app:**
- **Local-first:** Data resides on the user's device (local backup paths).
- **Metadata, not content:** The app searches for and organizes information about media, not the media itself.
- **Unified cross-platform:** A single codebase (Flutter) serves desktop and mobile.
- **Integration with established services:** Prefers public APIs and recognized tracking services.
- **Visual customization:** Supports visual boards, mood grids, and custom collections.
- **User privacy:** No proprietary cloud services are mentioned; backup is local.

**Guiding principle for suggestions:** Every suggestion must respect the distinction between **personal organization** (what Tonkatsu Box does) and **content access** (what the wikis index). No suggestion is made to transform Tonkatsu Box into a streaming, downloading, or reading client.

---

**Risk Note:** Third-party API integrations introduce external dependencies subject to TOS changes, rate limits, and discontinuation. An adapter pattern architecture is recommended to isolate these dependencies.

| 47 | **ROM metadata scraping by hash** (using No-Intro, Redump, TOSEC) | FMHY ROM resources |
| 48 | **Local playtime tracking** (integration with platform APIs or manual timers) | Steam, GOG Galaxy |

#### Anime/Manga
| # | Suggestion | Inspiration |
|---|------------|-------------|
| 49 | **Support for multiple manga readings:** tracking by chapter/volume with dates | MangaDex, MangaBaka already integrated; expand tracking |
| 50 | **"Filler episode" identification** for anime series | AnimeFillerList (FMHY) |
| 51 | **Watch order guides** for complex franchises (e.g., Fate, Monogatari) | watch_order, Chiaki (FMHY) |
| 52 | **Support for donghua/manhua/manhwa** as distinct categories with their own metadata | EverythingMoe categorization |

#### Books/Comics
| # | Suggestion | Inspiration |
|---|------------|-------------|
| 53 | **Support for comic metadata by issue** (not just by series/volume) | ComicVine already integrated; increase granularity |
| 54 | **Integration with Calibre** (import existing library) | FMHY reading / Calibre ecosystem |
| 55 | **Support for local EPUB/CBZ/CBR metadata reading** (without rendering content, just cataloging) | Ebook ecosystem |
| 56 | **Page reading tracking** for books and comics | Koodo, KOReader |

---

## 5. WARNINGS AND LIMITATIONS

1. **Third-party API dependencies:** Each new integration (RAWG, OpenCritic, SIMKL, etc.) introduces an external point of failure. Graceful degradation is recommended.
2. **Rate limiting:** Free APIs have strict limits. An app with many users could exceed them. Aggressive caching and possibly a custom proxy are suggested.
3. **Bidirectional sync complexity:** Sync with services like AniList or Trakt is technically more complex than one-way import due to conflict resolution.
4. **Legality of sources:** Although the wikis index many resources, not all APIs are equally permissive. Verify each API's TOS before implementation.
5. **Project scope:** Tonkatsu Box is a collection manager, not a player or download client. Suggestions that shift scope toward content consumption could compromise product clarity.
6. **Development resources:** As an open-source project, development bandwidth is limited. Prioritization is essential.

---

## 6. SUGGESTED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (Non-binding)

### Phase 1: Fundamentals (Low complexity, high impact)
- Custom statuses (#11)
- Tags/colors (#12)
- Activity heatmap (#19)
- Keyboard shortcuts (#40)
- List view (#39)
- Letterboxd import (#21)
- CSV/JSON export (#24)

### Phase 2: Metadata enrichment (Medium complexity)
- RAWG.io integration (#1)
- SIMKL integration (#10)
- Trailers/teasers (#31)
- Advanced statistics (#18)
- Basic recommendations (#30)
- Granular manga/anime tracking (#49)

### Phase 3: Ecosystem and extensibility (High complexity)
- Plugin system (#34)
- Bidirectional synchronization (#25)
- Local API (#35)
- P2P/cloud sync (#37)
- Calibre integration (#54)

---

## 7. DECLARATION OF UNCERTAINTY

- Complexity estimates are **opinionated** and based on general Flutter experience; they have not been verified against the specific Tonkatsu Box codebase.
- Availability and TOS of the mentioned APIs may change. Individual verification before implementation is recommended.
- No visibility into the author's internal roadmap exists. Some suggestions may already be planned or explicitly rejected.
- Architecture suggestions (plugins, local API, sync) are **exploratory** and would require deeper technical feasibility analysis.

titulo: 📚 The task of adding numerous mangas or updating a considerable volume of titles in the library is excessively slow. 😩
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature

📈 I propose a series of comprehensive reforms to the metadata management system for manga, aimed at optimizing both the acquisition process and the updating of information. Instead of requiring the manual insertion of metadata for each work in the various formats used, I suggest implementing an informative identifier system backed by artificial intelligence 🤖. This approach is akin to the model adopted by Yokai and should enable a more efficient and less resource-intensive management. As a result, this would facilitate the agile integration of new titles into our database, as well as the effective updating of existing titles 📚.

Additionally, I consider it essential to conduct a preliminary analysis of information from the formats used, in order to reduce the time it takes for the library to acquire new information ⏱️. This initial analysis could be customized according to user preferences, allowing them to choose between a comprehensive analysis that collects detailed data or a more superficial one that consumes fewer resources. This duality would resemble the error reporting system we currently send to your team 🛠️. The main difference between both types of analysis would lie in the amount of information retained in the system. While the deep analysis would store data more comprehensively on the application’s disk, the minimal analysis would focus on retaining only essential information, resulting in a more agile and lightweight application performance ⚡.

Regarding deep analysis, I propose that, once completed, an intelligent filtering of the information be carried out to help optimize future data collections 🔍. However, it is crucial to establish an automatic cleaning procedure to prevent storage saturation, as uncontrolled data accumulation could hinder system performance 🚫. Maintaining optimal performance is essential, and proper data management is key to ensuring that the application runs smoothly 🛡️.

Concerning the update of metadata through artificial intelligence, this method should be designed to be less resource-intensive 🔧. It would operate without the need to store permanent caches or extremely detailed data, retaining only the essential elements. In this way, whenever an update is generated, the system would reset using the most recent information, optimizing its operation thanks to a centralized database that prevents information overflow 🌊.

On another note, I wish to emphasize the importance of improving the accuracy of predictions regarding the publication dates of mangas already present in our library 📅. One highly beneficial option could be the ability to merge information from third-party sources with data from official platforms, such as AniList. Ideally, users should have the flexibility to enable or disable this option, giving them greater control over the management of information related to their favorite titles 🖊️.

In summary, these proposals aim to build a more agile and efficient system that not only simplifies metadata management but also offers users customizable options that adapt to their needs and preferences 🛠️. By doing so, the overall user experience will significantly improve, creating a more satisfying and dynamic environment that fosters interaction and enjoyment of our manga catalog 📖. With the implementation of these improvements, I hope that we can develop a solution that is not only reactive to changes in the market but also proactive in seeking to provide quality service that meets our users' expectations 🎯.

### Other details

😊 I kindly urge your consideration regarding my request. 🙏 I thank you in advance for your attention and regret having resorted to the assistance of artificial intelligence for the writing, due to my limitations in English proficiency and deficiencies in my writing skills. 🌟 God bless you; I express my sincere gratitude for your understanding. 💖 I hope the DMCA does not cause you any inconvenience. 📜

titulo: '5 Minimalist Evolution Improvements: Zen Mode, Smart Categories, WebDAV Wizard, Offline Batch, and Double Page View.'
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature

🔮 Las 5 Sugerencias (Detalladas)

🧘 1. Modo Zen Ultra-Minimalista

Cómo debería funcionar:

· Un toggle en el lector (quizás en el menú de ajustes rápidos) que active el "Modo Zen"
· Cuando está activo: oculta todos los elementos de UI (barra de progreso, contador de páginas, indicadores de capítulo)
· Los controles reaparecen solo con un toque breve en el centro de la pantalla
· Se desactiva automáticamente al salir del capítulo o con un gesto específico (pellizco para salir)
· Por qué es coherente: No es una función nueva; es la culminación lógica del lector edge-to-edge recién implementado. Es para esos momentos en los que quieres desaparecer del mundo por completo.

🏷️ 2. Sugerencias de Categorías Inteligentes

Cómo debería funcionar:

· Cuando añades un manga a la biblioteca, Komikku analiza sus tags/géneros de la fuente
· Muestra una notificación discreta: "¿Mover 'One Piece' a categoría 'Shonen'? [Sí/No]"
· Opcional y desactivable por defecto en ajustes
· El aprendizaje es local: la app recuerda tus decisiones pero no envía datos a ningún lado
· Por qué es coherente: Es la extensión natural del sistema de sugerencias de fuentes. Aprendizaje automático al servicio del orden, nunca al revés.

🧭 3. Wizard Visual para WebDAV

Cómo debería funcionar:

· En Ajustes > Sincronización > WebDAV, un botón "Configuración Guiada"
· Flujo paso a paso:
  1. "¿Usas Nextcloud, OwnCloud, Seafile u otro?" (con logos)
  2. "Ingresa la URL de tu servidor" (con ejemplos visuales)
  3. "Ingresa usuario y contraseña"
  4. Prueba automática de conexión con indicador visual
  5. "¡Listo! Tu biblioteca ahora se sincroniza entre dispositivos"
· Por qué es coherente: WebDAV es libertad pura, pero la primera configuración asusta a algunos. Hacer simple lo poderoso es el núcleo de Komikku.

📦 4. Lectura en Lote Offline

Cómo debería funcionar:

· En la pantalla de un manga, junto a "Descargar capítulo", un botón "Preparar para viaje"
· Al pulsar: "¿Descargar los próximos 10 capítulos? Te avisaremos cuando estén listos"
· La descarga ocurre en segundo plano con prioridad baja (no interrumpe uso normal)
· Notificación cuando está completo: "¡Listo para leer offline! Los capítulos se auto-limpiarán tras leer"
· Por qué es coherente: Aprovecha la auto-limpieza existente y resuelve un patrón común (viajes, zonas sin conexión) sin añadir complejidad permanente.

🖼️ 5. Vista Doble Página Inteligente

Cómo debería funcionar:

· Detección automática basada en:
  · Relación de aspecto de las páginas (manga vs cómic occidental)
  · Metadatos de la fuente cuando están disponibles
  · Configuración manual opcional por manga
· Cuando detecta cómic occidental: muestra páginas pareadas automáticamente
· Gestos para alternar entre vista simple/doble
· Mejor manejo nativo de PDF/CBR (manteniendo el excelente soporte actual de CBZ)
· Por qué es coherente: Respeta los formatos, no lucha contra ellos. Hace que Komikku sea aún más universal sin perder simplicidad.

### Other details

⚖️ Coherencia con la Filosofía Komikku

Todas estas sugerencias comparten estos principios:

1. Opcionales por defecto: Ninguna cambia el comportamiento actual a menos que el usuario lo active
2. Minimalismo en implementación: Interfaces limpias, sin menús anidados complejos
3. Aprovechan lo existente: Extienden funciones ya presentes (edge-to-edge, auto-limpieza, sugerencias)
4. Respetan la privacidad: Todo el procesamiento es local cuando sea posible
5. Mantienen la velocidad: No añaden latencia perceptible a la experiencia actual

---

📝 Additional details and attachments

🎯 Priorización Sugerida

1. Modo Zen (más simple, mayor impacto en experiencia)
2. Wizard WebDAV (reduce fricción para una función clave)
3. Lectura en Lote (automatiza patrón común)
4. Categorías Inteligentes (mejora organización sin esfuerzo)
5. Vista Doble Página (amplía alcance de formatos)

🔧 Consideraciones Técnicas

· Modo Zen: Requeriría ajustes en reader.kt pero reutiliza el sistema edge-to-edge
· Wizard WebDAV: Podría usar librerías existentes para autodetección de servidores
· Lectura en Lote: Se integra con el sistema de descargas existente y notificaciones
· Todas mantienen compatibilidad con versiones anteriores y no rompen funcionalidad actual

🌟 Impacto Esperado

· Retención de nuevos usuarios: Wizard WebDAV reduce la curva inicial
· Satisfacción de usuarios avanzados: Modo Zen y vista doble página cubren necesidades específicas
· Usabilidad universal: Mejor soporte de formatos atrae más tipos de lectores
· Fidelización: Automatización inteligente (categorías, lotes) hace que usuarios no quieran irse

📚 Inspiración y Referencias

· El Modo Zen se inspira en aplicaciones de lectura premium como Moon+ Reader
· El Wizard WebDAV sigue patrones de usabilidad de Nextcloud/ownCloud apps
· La detección de formato existe en aplicaciones como Perfect Viewer y CDisplayEx
· Todas las sugerencias mantienen el espíritu minimalista que hace único a Komikku

titulo: 🎯 Issue 2: [SUGERENCIA] Sugerencias de Categorías Inteligentes
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature



Título: [SUGERENCIA] Sugerencias de Categorías Inteligentes - Organización automática local

---

📋 Describe your suggested feature

🎯 Contexto y Filosofía

Komikku ya tiene un sistema brillante de sugerencias de fuentes que elimina la gestión manual de extensiones. Las Sugerencias de Categorías Inteligentes extienden esta filosofía al ámbito de la organización: usar la inteligencia local para proponer orden sin imponerlo, respetando siempre la decisión final del usuario.

🏷️ Sugerencias de Categorías Inteligentes - Funcionamiento Propuesto

Cómo debería funcionar:

1. Detección inteligente:
   · Cuando añades un manga a tu biblioteca, Komikku analiza sus metadatos (géneros, tags, demografía)
   · Compara con categorías existentes en tu biblioteca
   · Identifica patrones: "Este manga tiene tags [Shonen, Acción, Aventura]"
2. Sugerencia discreta:
   · Notificación no intrusiva: "¿Mover 'One Piece' a categoría 'Shonen'? [Sí/No]"
   · Aparece una vez, no se repite si ignoras
   · Opción "No preguntar de nuevo para este género" disponible
3. Aprendizaje local:
   · Cero datos en la nube: Todo procesamiento ocurre en el dispositivo
   · Aprende de tus decisiones: si siempre aceptas "Shonen → Shonen", deja de preguntar
   · Base de datos local de asociaciones usuario-género-categoría
4. Configuración respetuosa:
   · Desactivado por defecto: No cambia comportamiento sin permiso
   · Opción en Ajustes → Biblioteca → "Sugerencias de categorías"
   · Puedes borrar historial de aprendizaje en cualquier momento

Por qué es coherente con Komikku:

· Extensión natural del sistema de sugerencias de fuentes
· Aprendizaje automático al servicio del orden, nunca al revés
· Resuelve un problema real (bibliotecas desorganizadas) sin crear fricción
· Respeta privacidad absoluta: todo ocurre localmente
· Mantiene control total del usuario: sugiere, no impone

---

📝 Additional details and attachments

🎯 Impacto Esperado

· Organización sin esfuerzo: Usuarios con bibliotecas grandes mantendrán orden naturalmente
· Descubrimiento mejorado: Agrupar por género facilita encontrar lecturas similares
· Retención de nuevos usuarios: Primeras impresiones de "app inteligente que me entiende"
· Reducción de abandono: Menos usuarios abandonan por "mi biblioteca es un caos"

🔧 Consideraciones Técnicas

· Análisis de metadatos: Usar genre, tag, demographic ya disponibles en fuentes
· Algoritmo simple: Reglas basadas en coincidencia de términos, no ML complejo
· Almacenamiento local: SharedPreferences o pequeña base de datos SQLite
· Ubicación en código: LibraryManager.kt - extensión del flujo de añadir manga
· Compatibilidad: Funciona con categorías existentes, no requiere cambios estructurales

### Describe your suggested feature



Título: [SUGERENCIA] Lectura en Lote Offline - "Preparar para Viaje"

---

📋 Describe your suggested feature

🎯 Contexto y Filosofía

Komikku ya tiene un excelente sistema de descargas y auto-limpieza. La Lectura en Lote Offline extiende esta funcionalidad para un caso de uso específico y común: prepararse para viajes largos o zonas sin conexión. Es la automatización inteligente de un patrón que muchos usuarios ya realizan manualmente, reduciendo fricción sin añadir complejidad permanente.

📦 Lectura en Lote Offline - Funcionamiento Propuesto

Cómo debería funcionar:

1. Acceso intuitivo:
   · En la pantalla de un manga, junto a "Descargar capítulo", botón "Preparar para viaje"
   · Icono distintivo (maleta o avión) que indica propósito específico
   · También accesible desde menú de opciones de la biblioteca
2. Configuración flexible:
   · Al pulsar: "¿Descargar los próximos 10 capítulos? Te avisaremos cuando estén listos"
   · Opciones rápidas: 5, 10, 15, 20 capítulos
   · Opción avanzada: "Descargar hasta el capítulo X" (selector numérico)
   · Configuración predeterminada ajustable en Ajustes → Descargas
3. Comportamiento inteligente:
   · Descarga en segundo plano con prioridad baja (no interrumpe uso normal)
   · Notificación progresiva: "Descargando 3/10 capítulos..."
   · Notificación final: "¡Listo para leer offline! Los capítulos se auto-limpiarán tras leer"
   · Gestión automática de espacio: Si dispositivo tiene poco espacio, sugiere reducir cantidad
4. Integración con sistema existente:
   · Usa el mismo sistema de descargas de Komikku (cola, reintentos, manejo de errores)
   · Respeta configuración existente (solo Wi-Fi, límites simultáneos, etc.)
   · Se integra con auto-limpieza: capítulos marcados para eliminación tras lectura

Por qué es coherente con Komikku:

· No añade complejidad: extiende funcionalidad existente (descargas + auto-limpieza)
· Resuelve un patrón real de uso (viajes, hospitales, zonas rurales)
· Mantiene minimalismo: una opción más, no nuevos menús anidados
· Es temporal y específica: no cambia comportamiento general de la app
· "Preparar para viaje" es más intuitivo que "descargar varios capítulos"

---

📝 Additional details and attachments

🎯 Impacto Esperado

· Usabilidad mejorada: Usuarios viajeros preparan lectura offline en 2 toques
· Reducción de errores: Menos usuarios descargan manualmente capítulos duplicados
· Retención: Usuarios atrapados sin conexión seguirán usando Komikku
· Diferenciación: Función práctica que resuelve necesidad real de nicho

🔧 Consideraciones Técnicas

· Integración con DownloadManager: Extender DownloadService.kt con modo "batch"
· Cola inteligente: Prioridad baja para no afectar experiencia actual
· Notificaciones: Usar NotificationCompat con progreso y acciones
· Gestión de espacio: StorageManager para verificar espacio disponible antes de empezar
· Persistencia: Guardar estado de descargas por lotes en SharedPreferences

📊 Flujo de Usuario Visual

```
[Usuario selecciona manga] → [Toca "Preparar para viaje"] → [Selector: 5,10,15,20 capítulos]
         ↓
[Confirmación] → [Descarga en background con prioridad baja]
         ↓
[Notificación progresiva] → [Finalización: "¡Listo! 10 capítulos descargados"]
         ↓
[Usuario viaja] → [Lee offline normalmente] → [Auto-limpieza tras lectura]
```

⚙️ Implementación Sugerida por Fases

Fase 1 (Mínimo Viable):

· Botón "Preparar para viaje" con opciones fijas (5,10,15)
· Descarga en segundo plano simple
· Notificación básica de progreso y finalización

Fase 2 (Mejoras):

· Selector numérico personalizado
· Gestión inteligente de espacio (advertencia si poco espacio)
· Reanudación si descarga se interrumpe
· Estadísticas: "X capítulos descargados para offline este mes"

Fase 3 (Avanzado):

· "Modo avión automático": Detecta próximos vuelos en calendario y sugiere preparación
· Compartir lote: "Enviar estos capítulos a otro dispositivo"
· Programación: "Preparar todos los sábados a las 20:00"
· Integración con apps de viaje (TripIt, Google Trips)

🧠 Casos de Uso Específicos

1. Viaje en avión:

· Usuario tiene vuelo de 4 horas → descarga 15 capítulos de una serie
· Lee durante el vuelo → capítulos se auto-limpián al terminar
· Al aterrizar, espacio liberado automáticamente

2. Zona rural sin internet:

· Usuario visita familia en pueblo sin buena conexión
· Prepara 20 capítulos de varias series
· Lee durante la semana → limpieza gradual según avanza

3. Hospital/espera:

· Usuario tiene cita médica larga
· Prepara 10 capítulos rápidamente
· Lee en sala de espera → capítulos se eliminan tras leer

🔗 Integración con Sistema Existente

```
"Preparar para viaje" → genera → Lista de capítulos → pasa a → DownloadManager
       ↓                                  ↓                          ↓
[Interfaz simple]           [Selección inteligente]       [Mismo sistema de siempre]
       ↓                                  ↓                          ↓
[Usuario contento]           [Sin duplicados]            [Gestión robusta de errores]
```

titulo: 📋 Suggestion #8: Offline Library with Smart Prefetch and Storage Optimization
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature



Current Problem:
Users who want to download chapters for offline reading either have to do it manually one by one, or risk running out of storage because downloaded chapters pile up unnoticed. There's no intelligent system to manage what gets saved and what gets cleaned.

Proposed Solution:
Implement a smart offline library with predictive prefetching and automated storage optimization.

Key Features:

· Smart Prefetch (AI-powered prediction):
  · Komikku learns your reading habits. If you always read the next chapter of a series within 24 hours, it automatically pre-downloads the next 3 chapters when you're on WiFi.
  · "I noticed you binge-read One Piece on weekends. Pre-download next 10 chapters every Friday?"
· Storage Health Dashboard:
  · Visual breakdown of downloaded content by series, with size indicators.
  · "You have 2.3GB of downloaded manga. 800MB hasn't been opened in 3 months."
· Intelligent Auto-Clean:
  · Configurable rules: "Delete chapters older than X days", "Keep only last Y chapters per series", "Never delete favorites".
  · One-tap "Clean Up" that suggests what to remove based on your actual reading.
· Selective Download Quality:
  · Download in "Reading quality" (high-res) for favorites, "Archival quality" (compressed) for everything else.
  · Auto-switch based on screen size: tablet gets high-res, phone gets optimized.
· Offline-First Mode:
  · When you're offline, Komikku automatically hides sources that require internet and shows only your downloaded library.
  · Seamless transition: open the app on a plane, and it just works with zero confusion.
· Cloud Backup Integration (Optional):
  · Users can optionally back up their downloaded library metadata to Google Drive/Dropbox.
  · If you reinstall, Komikku knows what you had downloaded and can re-download it intelligently.

Why it wins:

· Never run out of space: Storage is managed automatically, not manually.
· Always have something to read: Predictive downloads mean you rarely open the app offline and find nothing.
· Zero friction: Reading offline becomes as seamless as reading online.

Anizen focuses on streaming. Komikku can master the offline experience. 📚

titulo: 📋 Suggestion #9: Adaptive Reading Experience with Dynamic Profiles
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


Current Problem:
Komikku has great reading settings, but they're static. Users have to manually switch between "Webtoon mode" and "Classic manga mode" depending on what they're reading. Different genres, artists, or sources might benefit from different reading setups, but there's no way to automate this.

Proposed Solution:
Implement an adaptive reading system that automatically applies the optimal reading settings based on content type, source, and user behavior patterns.

Key Features:

· Auto-detect content format:
    Komikku analyzes the image dimensions and aspect ratios to automatically determine if you're reading:
  · Traditional manga (right-to-left, spreads, standard pages)
  · Webtoons (long vertical strips)
  · Western comics (left-to-right, color pages)
  · Light novels (text-heavy, needs different font/background)
· Dynamic reading profiles:
    Each format triggers the optimal reading configuration automatically:
  · Manga mode: Right-to-left paging, spread detection, page crop
  · Webtoon mode: Vertical continuous scroll, lazy loading, optimized caching
  · Comic mode: Left-to-right, fit to width, color enhancement
  · Novel mode: Custom text size, line spacing, night mode with sepia
· Source-specific presets:
    Users can assign default reading modes to specific extensions.
    "Always open chapters from AnimeFLV in Webtoon mode."
· Learning algorithm:
    Komikku watches how you manually adjust settings and learns your preferences over time.
    "I noticed you always switch to Webtoon mode when reading Tower of God. Should I do this automatically?"
· Per-chapter memory:
    If you read a specific series in a particular way, Komikku remembers that format even if you switch devices.
· Quick-switch overlay:
    While reading, a subtle overlay lets you temporarily override the current mode without diving into settings.

Why it wins:

· Zero friction: You never have to remember to switch modes. Komikku just knows.
· Personalized: The app adapts to YOU, not the other way around.
· Format-aware: Different content gets the treatment it deserves.

Anizen focuses on finding content. Komikku can perfect how you CONSUME it. 📖

titulo: 🎯 Suggestion #4 for Komikku: Komikku Community Hub (In-App Social)
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


Current Problem:
The Komikku community is scattered across Discord, Telegram, Reddit, and GitHub. Users have to leave the app to ask questions, share discoveries, report broken sources, or find recommendations. This fragmentation makes the community feel less connected and slows down problem-solving. New users struggle to find the best sources or setups.

Proposed Solution:
Build an integrated community hub directly inside the Komikku app, turning it from a simple reader into a social ecosystem where manga lovers connect, share, and help each other.

Key Features:

· Community feed:
  · Scrollable timeline showing recent discussions, tips, and announcements from developers.
  · Highlights from power users sharing their library setups and reading lists.
  · "Manga of the Day" curated by community votes.
· Crowdsourced source health:
  · Users can report if a source is working, slow, or down for them.
  · See real-time status with color coding:
        🟢 "87 users report this source working"
        🟡 "23 users report slow loading"
        🔴 "12 users report source down"
  · Historical reliability scores for each extension (weekly/monthly uptime %).
· Shareable configuration codes:
  · Export your entire extension setup, categories, and reading preferences as a single code/QR.
  · Share with friends: "Here's my perfect setup for reading One Piece, Jujutsu Kaisen, and Solo Leveling."
  · Import someone else's curated configuration in one tap – perfect for new users.
· Community recommendations:
  · User-generated reading lists: "Top 10 hidden gems according to the community."
  · "What others are reading" section showing trending manga in your region.
  · Follow specific users whose taste matches yours and see their updates.
· Extension voting system:
  · Users can vote on which extensions they want prioritized for updates.
  · Developers see community demand at a glance.
  · "Most requested" section in the extension repo guides development priorities.
· In-app announcements:
  · No more searching GitHub for changelogs. Updates appear right in the app.
  · Push notifications for critical updates: "AnimeFLV extension fixed – update now to restore access."
  · Changelog summaries in plain language, not just code commits.
· Community troubleshooting:
  · Built-in FAQ and knowledge base with solutions to common problems.
  · Users can mark helpful solutions, surfacing the best answers to the top.
  · Optional anonymous error reporting to help developers fix issues faster.
· Reading groups (optional):
  · Create or join groups reading the same manga.
  · Chapter discussion threads integrated directly into the reader.
  · "24 people in the 'Jujutsu Kaisen' group just finished Chapter 245. Join the discussion?"

Why it's a game changer:
The community lives INSIDE Komikku. Questions get answered faster, problems get reported instantly, and users feel connected without ever leaving the app. New users go from "how do I set this up?" to "I have the perfect configuration" in minutes thanks to shared codes. It transforms Komikku from a tool into a destination – a home for manga lovers. 🌐

titulo: 🎯 SUGGESTION #1 FOR ANIZEN: EPIC GITHUB-STYLE STATISTICS + SPOTIFY WRAPPED
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


---

📉 Current Problem

Anizen already has basic statistics (episodes watched, time spent, etc.), but their presentation is... well, basic. Users can't easily visualize their viewing habits, track streaks, discover their favorite genres, or share achievements. The data exists, but it's buried and not engaging.

💡 Proposed Solution

Transform the statistics screen into an interactive dashboard that makes data exploration fun, insightful, and shareable.

Key Features:

1. GitHub-Style Contribution Graph

· A heat grid showing which days you watched anime.
· Color intensity based on number of episodes watched per day.
· Current streak and longest streak prominently displayed.
· Monthly/yearly views.

2. Global Statistics

· Total episodes watched (lifetime, by month, by year).
· Total estimated viewing time (e.g., "You've watched the equivalent of 23 days straight").
· Completion rate vs. dropped rate.
· Average episodes per day/week/month.

3. Genre Breakdown

· Interactive pie chart showing your most-watched genres (shonen, seinen, romance, slice of life, etc.).
· Based on metadata from extensions (when available).
· Genre trends over time: "You switched from shonen to seinen in March 2025."

4. Hourly Heatmap

· What time of day do you watch most? Are you a night owl or morning viewer?
· Helps users understand their own habits.

5. Source Performance Stats

· Which extensions you use most frequently.
· Average latency per source over time (integrated with Extension Health).
· Success rate (% of episodes that loaded without errors).

6. Achievements & Milestones

· Unlockable badges: "Century Club" (100 episodes), "Binge Master" (50 episodes in one day), "Explorer" (used 10+ different sources), etc.
· Milestone notifications: "Congratulations! You've watched 500 episodes this year!"

7. Year in Review (Spotify Wrapped Style)

· At the end of each year, generate a beautiful, shareable summary.
· Include: total episodes, top genres, longest binge, favorite source, viewing streaks, and more.
· Shareable cards for social media (Twitter, Instagram, etc.) – great for spreading Anizen's name organically.

8. Exportable Data

· Users can export their complete viewing history as CSV/JSON.
· Full ownership of personal data.

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

✅ HIGHLY FEASIBLE. CMK explicitly said: "Most of this is already in statistics. I can upgrade them." The data already exists locally; it just needs better presentation and some additional calculations.

What's already there:

· Episode watch history (timestamps, series, episode numbers).
· Source usage data.
· Basic counts.

What needs to be added:

· Genre extraction from extension metadata.
· More sophisticated calculations (streaks, trends, etc.).
· Beautiful UI components (charts, graphs, heatmaps).
· Export functionality.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

1. Audit existing data: Review what's already stored in the local database and what needs to be added.
2. Design UI/UX: Create mockups inspired by GitHub contributions, Spotify Wrapped, and fitness apps.
3. Choose charting libraries: Consider MPAndroidChart, Canvas, or custom Compose components.
4. Implement achievement system: Create triggers for milestones (e.g., "episode count reaches 100").
5. Build Year in Review generator: Logic to compile stats at year-end and generate shareable images.
6. Add export functionality: JSON/CSV export with proper formatting.

---

🎉 User Benefits

· Self-discovery: Users learn fascinating things about their own habits.
· Motivation: Streaks and achievements encourage daily engagement.
· Community: Year in Review reports will go viral on social media, giving Anizen free publicity.
· Data ownership: Users can export and analyze their own data.

---

### Describe your suggested feature



📉 Current Problem

Users who travel, commute, or have unstable internet connections need to manually switch to offline mode. The process is tedious, easy to forget, and often remembered only when it's too late — right when you're on a subway with no signal and nothing downloaded. Currently, Anizen requires manual intervention to switch between online and offline states.

💡 Proposed Solution

Implement an intelligent but configurable offline mode that avoids false positives and gives users complete control over how and when the app switches to offline state.

Key Features:

1. Manual Activation (Default)

· A prominent "Offline Mode" toggle button on the main screen or quick settings.
· When activated, the app immediately hides all streaming sources and shows only downloaded content.
· Visual indicator (icon/color change) clearly shows when offline mode is active.

2. Configurable Automatic Activation

In Settings → Offline Mode, users can enable optional automatic switching with parameters:

Setting Options Default
Auto-switch to offline On/Off Off
Connection loss threshold 5s, 10s, 30s, 60s, 2min 30s
Auto-switch back to online Immediately / Ask first / Never Ask first
Only activate on certain networks WiFi only / Any network Any network

3. Smart Time Threshold

· Instead of switching the instant internet drops (which would cause chaos with unstable connections), Anizen waits for a user-defined period of continuous disconnection.
· Example: "If no internet for 30 seconds, ask if I want to switch to offline mode."
· This prevents flickering between modes during brief connection drops.

4. Offline-First Interface

When offline mode is active:

· All streaming sources are hidden from the UI.
· Library view filters to show ONLY series with downloaded episodes.
· Search functionality limited to downloaded content.
· Clear messaging: "You're in offline mode. Connect to internet to access streaming sources."

5. Smart Download Suggestions (Integrated with Suggestion #7)

· When offline mode activates, Anizen can suggest: "You have 5 unwatched downloaded episodes. Would you like to prioritize these?"
· If no downloads exist: "You're offline with no downloads. Connect to WiFi to download episodes for next time."

6. Offline Indicator Everywhere

· A persistent icon in the status bar showing current mode (online/offline).
· Color-coded: 🟢 Online, 🟡 Weak connection, 🔴 Offline.

7. Background Sync When Back Online

· When reconnecting, Anizen can optionally sync progress and check for new episodes automatically.
· User configurable: "Sync immediately / Ask first / Don't sync automatically."

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

⚠️ POSSIBLE BUT REQUIRES CAREFUL IMPLEMENTATION. CMK explicitly warned: "I can do that automatic offline mode but this would arise like if your internet is unstable or something."

The key is making it configurable rather than purely automatic. By giving users control over thresholds and behavior, we avoid the negative experiences CMK is concerned about.

What's already there:

· Anizen can detect network connectivity changes.
· The app knows which episodes are downloaded locally.
· Download system already exists.

What needs to be added:

· Time-based threshold logic.
· Configurable settings UI.
· Offline/online state management that doesn't interfere with streaming.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Core Infrastructure

1. Robust connectivity detector: Use ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback (API 21+) for real-time, accurate network changes (more reliable than old broadcast receivers).
2. State management: Create a central ConnectivityState class that tracks:
   · Current connection status (none, mobile, WiFi)
   · Duration of disconnection
   · User's offline mode preference

Phase 2: Threshold Logic

1. Timer implementation: When disconnection detected, start a timer based on user's configured threshold.
2. Cancel logic: If connection returns before timer expires, cancel and do nothing.
3. Trigger action: If timer expires, execute user's preference:
   · Auto-switch to offline
   · Show dialog asking user
   · Do nothing (manual only)

Phase 3: UI Integration

1. Persistent indicator: Add status bar icon and quick settings tile (if possible).
2. Offline mode UI: Modify library views to filter by download status.
3. Settings screen: Create comprehensive offline settings with all configurable options.

Phase 4: Smart Features

1. Download suggestions: Integrate with download manager to suggest content when entering offline mode with no downloads.
2. Background sync: Add optional auto-sync when reconnecting.

---

⚠️ Edge Cases to Handle

Edge Case Proposed Solution
Unstable connection (flickering on/off) Time threshold prevents switching until stable loss
User manually overrides Manual toggle always takes priority
No downloaded content at all Offline mode still works (empty state with helpful message)
Partial downloads Mark episodes as "partially downloaded" and handle gracefully
Multiple users on same device Settings per user profile (if supported)

---

🎉 User Benefits

· Peace of mind: Never get caught without content when internet disappears.
· Control: Users decide exactly how aggressive or conservative the offline switching should be.
· No false positives: Time thresholds prevent annoying switches during brief connection drops.
· Clear communication: Visual indicators always show current state.
· Smooth experience: Offline mode feels native, not like an afterthought.

---

📊 Comparison with Current Behavior

Scenario Current Behavior With This Feature
Enter subway with no signal App tries to load, fails, user confused After 30s, switches to offline, shows downloads only
Unstable 3G connection Constant buffering, app unresponsive Stays online (threshold not reached), but could suggest offline mode
User wants offline only Must remember to toggle manually One tap toggle, or set auto-switch with threshold
Reconnect after being offline Manual refresh needed Optional auto-sync of progress and new episodes

---

🎯 Why This Matters

This feature transforms Anizen from a streaming app into a true offline companion. It acknowledges that real-world connectivity is messy and gives users the tools to handle it gracefully. Combined with smart download suggestions (Suggestion #7), it creates a seamless experience whether you're on WiFi, mobile data, or 30 meters underground.

---

#Anizen #FeatureRequest #OfflineMode #SmartOffline #Configurable #UserExperience #Connectivity #OfflineFirst

titulo: 🎯 SUGGESTION #3 FOR ANIZEN: CLOUD SYNC (BACKUP & CROSS-DEVICE)
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


---

📉 Current Problem

Users who switch phones, use multiple devices (phone + tablet), or need to reinstall the app lose all their carefully curated configuration: extensions, custom order, episode progress, categories, and personalized settings. Manual backups are tedious, often forgotten, and sometimes fail to restore everything perfectly. Currently, there's no seamless way to maintain a consistent Anizen experience across devices.

💡 Proposed Solution

Implement optional cloud synchronization using third-party services (Google Drive, Dropbox, Nextcloud) to backup and sync user configuration and progress.

Key Features:

1. Complete Profile Sync (Metadata Only)

Sync everything except actual downloaded files:

Data Type Sync? Notes
Installed extensions & order ✅ Yes Complete list with preferences
Episode progress ✅ Yes Which episodes watched, position
Library categories ✅ Yes Custom categories and organization
App settings ✅ Yes All user preferences
Watch history ✅ Yes Timestamps, series, episodes
Downloaded files metadata ✅ Yes Pointers to what's downloaded (not the files themselves)
Actual downloaded files ❌ No Too large for cloud storage

2. Multiple Cloud Options

· Google Drive (primary, most common on Android)
· Dropbox (secondary)
· Nextcloud (for self-hosted privacy enthusiasts)
· Local network sync (WiFi direct between devices) – advanced option

3. Sync Modes

Mode Description Use Case
Manual User triggers sync with one tap Simple backup before reinstalling
Automatic (on change) Syncs after significant actions (new episode watched, extension added) Real-time cross-device sync
WiFi-only Restrict automatic sync to WiFi Save mobile data
Scheduled Daily/weekly backups Peace of mind

4. Smart Conflict Resolution

When changes happen on two devices while offline:

Conflict Type Resolution Strategy
Same episode watched on both Merge (keep both marks if different episodes, or use latest timestamp)
Different settings Show diff with options: [Keep Device A] [Keep Device B] [Merge]
Extension lists differ Union of both lists with duplicate removal
Category organization Ask user which version to keep

5. End-to-End Encryption

· All data encrypted locally before uploading.
· Encryption key derived from user's account (never sent to server).
· Even cloud providers cannot read your data.

6. New Device Setup Wizard

When Anizen detects first run on a new device:

```
Welcome to Anizen!

[ ] Restore from cloud backup
[ ] Start fresh

If you choose restore:
- Select cloud provider
- Sign in
- Choose which backup to restore (list with timestamps)
- 2 minutes later, your new device looks EXACTLY like your old one
```

7. Backup History

· Keep multiple backups (last 5, configurable).
· View backup details: size, date, included data.
· Restore from any point in time.

8. Selective Sync

· Choose which categories sync (e.g., "Currently Watching" syncs, "Completed" doesn't).
· Exclude large metadata from certain sources if desired.

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

✅ FEASIBLE. CMK mentioned: "All of this would be possible if we have one database and direct api." While we don't have our own API, we can leverage existing cloud storage APIs (Google Drive, Dropbox) to store encrypted configuration files.

What's already there:

· Anizen has a complete local database of user data.
· Serialization/deserialization of app state is possible.

What needs to be added:

· Integration with cloud provider APIs.
· Encryption layer.
· Conflict resolution UI.
· Sync scheduling and management.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Foundation

1. Data serialization: Create a comprehensive data class that represents the entire user profile:
   ```kotlin
   data class AnizenProfile(
       val version: Int,
       val extensions: List<Extension>,
       val extensionOrder: List<String>,
       val progress: Map<SeriesId, EpisodeProgress>,
       val categories: List<Category>,
       val settings: AppSettings,
       val history: List<WatchEvent>,
       val timestamp: Long
   )
   ```
2. Serialization format: Use Protocol Buffers or compressed JSON for efficiency.
3. Encryption layer: Implement AES-256 encryption using a key derived from user's cloud account (deterministic).

Phase 2: Cloud Integration (Start Simple)

1. Google Drive integration first (most common):
   · Implement Google Sign-In.
   · Create hidden app folder in user's Drive.
   · Upload/download encrypted profile files.
2. Basic manual backup/restore:
   · Settings screen option: "Backup to Drive"
   · "Restore from Drive" with list of available backups.

Phase 3: Advanced Sync

1. Automatic sync triggers:
   · After episode marked watched
   · After extension changes
   · On app close (with debounce)
2. Conflict resolution UI:
   · Simple dialog when conflicts detected.
   · Option to preview differences before choosing.
3. Additional cloud providers: Add Dropbox, Nextcloud based on demand.

Phase 4: Polish

1. Backup history management: Allow users to delete old backups.
2. Selective sync options: UI for choosing what syncs automatically.
3. Progress indicators: Show sync status with animations.

---

⚠️ Privacy & Security Considerations

Concern Solution
User data on third-party servers End-to-end encryption before upload
Cloud provider access Only encrypted blobs, no readable data
Account compromise Encryption key not stored in cloud
Government requests Nothing readable to hand over
User wants to delete all data Clear option to delete all remote backups

---

🎉 User Benefits

· True multi-device experience: Phone for commuting, tablet for home, perfectly synchronized.
· Never lose your setup: Switch phones without losing a single setting.
· Peace of mind: Automatic backups mean you can always restore.
· Share configurations: (Future) Export your setup as a link for friends to import.
· Data ownership: Your data, your encryption, your control.

---

📊 Comparison with Current Workarounds

Current Workaround Problems Cloud Sync Solution
Manual backup/restore (JSON) Easy to forget, manual steps Automatic, seamless
Third-party backup apps May not capture all data Complete profile sync
Multiple devices manual sync Impossible to maintain Real-time sync
Starting fresh on new phone Lose everything One-tap restore

---

🎯 Why This Matters

This feature transforms Anizen from a single-device app into a cross-platform ecosystem. Users become loyal because their investment in configuration and progress is preserved forever. It's the difference between an app you use and an app that becomes part of your daily life.

---

🏷️ Hashtags

#Anizen #FeatureRequest #CloudSync #Backup #CrossDevice #GoogleDrive #Dropbox #DataOwnership #Privacy

---
