titulo: 🎯 SUGGESTION #4 FOR ANIZEN: SMART LIBRARY WITH AUTOMATIC CATEGORIES
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


---

📉 Current Problem

Users have to manually organize their 50+ anime titles into categories. Every time they add a new series, they have to remember to put it in the right folder. This is tedious, time‑consuming, and easy to forget – leading to a messy, unorganized library that's hard to navigate. Over time, the library becomes chaotic, and users lose track of what they're watching, what's new, and what they've abandoned.

💡 Proposed Solution

Implement an auto‑organizing library system that automatically classifies anime based on user‑defined rules and intelligent detection, keeping the library clean with zero manual effort.

Key Features:

1. Customizable Rules Engine

Users can create simple "if‑then" rules to automate organization:

Rule Type Example
By genre "If genre contains 'shonen', move to 'Currently Watching' category"
By source "If from AnimeFLV extension, add to 'Spanish Dubbed' category"
By status "If episode progress < 3, keep in 'Just Started' category"
By tags "If series has 'completed' tag, move to 'Finished' category"
By season "If release year = 2025, add to 'New Season' category"
By rating "If user rating > 4 stars, add to 'Favorites' automatically"

Rule Builder Interface:

· Simple dropdown menus for conditions and actions.
· AND/OR logic for complex rules.
· Preview of how many series would be affected.
· Test button to simulate rule without applying.

2. Automatic Status Detection

Anizen tracks your progress and automatically categorizes based on activity:

Status Detection Logic
Currently Watching Watched at least one episode in last 7 days
On Hold No activity for 14+ days but series not completed
Completed All available episodes watched
Plan to Watch Added but never started
Dropped User manually marked as dropped OR no activity for 60+ days (configurable)
Hiatus No new episodes for 30+ days (source-dependent)

3. Smart Season Grouping

If you add Jujutsu Kaisen Season 2, Anizen automatically:

· Detects it's the same series as Season 1.
· Groups them under a parent entry.
· Shows season selection when opening.
· Combined progress tracking across seasons.

No more separate, unrelated entries cluttering your library.

4. Dynamic Smart Categories (AI‑Powered)

Categories that update automatically based on context:

Dynamic Category What It Shows
🔔 New Episodes Series with episodes released in last 24 hours
🔥 Trending in Your Region Based on crowdsourced popularity (see Suggestion #6)
🎯 Because You Watched... Recommendations based on your history
⏰ Almost Forgotten Series you haven't touched in 30+ days
📊 Most Bingeable Completed series with 50+ chapters you haven't started
⭐ Fan Favorites Top-rated series in your library

5. Integration with Extension Health

If a source is slow or down, the smart library can:

· Automatically suggest moving affected titles to alternative sources.
· Show warning badges on series affected by source issues.
· Prioritize migration for series with new episodes stuck on dead sources.

6. One‑Click Reorganization

A "Clean Up My Library" button that:

· Applies all your rules to fix miscategorized entries.
· Merges duplicate series from different sources.
· Removes empty categories.
· Shows a summary of changes made.

7. Visual Indicators

Small badges on each anime cover showing:

· Current category color coding.
· Source health status (🟢/🟡/🔴).
· New episode count.
· Watch status (progress bar overlay).

8. Category Templates

Pre‑built rule sets users can enable with one tap:

Template What It Does
"The Completionist" Tracks everything meticulously, creates separate categories for each status
"The Casual Viewer" Simple: Currently Watching, Completed, Plan to Watch only
"The Genre Explorer" Auto‑categorizes by detected genres
"The Language Learner" Separates by audio/subtitle language
"The Data Saver" Prioritizes sources with lower bandwidth usage

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

✅ HIGHLY FEASIBLE. CMK did not express any technical objections to this type of feature. The app already has:

· Local database of series with metadata.
· Episode progress tracking.
· Source information for each series.
· User preference storage.

What needs to be added:

· Rule evaluation engine.
· Genre detection from extension metadata.
· More sophisticated progress analysis.
· Category management system.

Complexity Level: Moderate. This is primarily UI/UX work plus a rule engine, no deep system-level changes required.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Foundation

1. Database schema expansion: Add tables for:
   · user_rules (id, condition_json, action_json, enabled)
   · dynamic_categories (predefined smart categories)
   · series_metadata_cache (store genres, tags, etc.)
2. Rule engine core:
   ```kotlin
   interface Rule {
       fun evaluate(series: Series): Boolean
       fun apply(series: Series): Category?
   }
   ```
   Implement simple parser for user-defined conditions.

Phase 2: Status Detection

1. Progress analyzer: Create a service that runs periodically (or on app open) to:
   · Calculate last watch dates.
   · Detect inactivity thresholds.
   · Update series status flags.
2. Season detection algorithm: Compare series titles and metadata to identify related seasons.

Phase 3: UI Implementation

1. Rule builder interface:
   · Dropdown selectors for conditions and actions.
   · Preview area showing affected series.
   · Save/load/edit rules.
2. Category view updates:
   · Modify library screen to show dynamic categories.
   · Add visual badges and indicators.
   · Implement drag‑and‑drop for manual override.

Phase 4: Smart Features

1. Integration with Extension Health: Add callbacks to trigger category updates when source health changes.
2. Recommendation engine: Simple collaborative filtering based on user's history.
3. Cleanup wizard: Batch operation UI with preview.

---

📊 Example Rule Scenarios

User Goal Rule Configuration
"I only want to see ongoing series first" IF status = "ONGOING" AND progress < total_episodes THEN move to "Currently Watching (Priority)"
"Separate anime by language automatically" IF source.name contains "Latino" THEN add to "Spanish Dubbed"
"Keep completed series out of my main view" IF progress = total_episodes THEN move to "Completed" category AND hide from main feed
"Never lose track of series I've abandoned" IF last_watch_days > 30 AND progress < total_episodes THEN move to "Abandoned" AND notify me

---

🎉 User Benefits

· Zero manual organization: Library stays clean automatically.
· Always find what to watch: Smart categories highlight fresh content.
· Rediscover forgotten series: "Almost Forgotten" category reminds you of abandoned shows.
· Perfect for large libraries: Scales to 100+ series without chaos.
· Personalized: Rules adapt to your preferences, not a one‑size‑fits‑all solution.

---

🎯 Why This Matters

This feature transforms the library from a static list into a living, breathing collection that adapts to user behavior. It solves the "library decay" problem that plagues every media app after months of use. Users stay engaged because their library always feels fresh and organized, without any effort on their part.

---

🏷️ Hashtags

#Anizen #FeatureRequest #SmartLibrary #AutoCategories #LibraryManagement #RulesEngine #Personalization

---

titulo: 🎯 SUGGESTION #5 FOR ANIZEN: SMART PLAYBACK WITH AUTOMATIC QUALITY PROFILES
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


---

📉 Current Problem

Users manually choose video quality every time they start an episode, or they leave a fixed setting that doesn't adapt to changing conditions. On mobile data they want to save bandwidth, on WiFi they want maximum quality, and when battery is low they'd prefer lower quality to extend playback. Switching back and forth manually is a constant annoyance that interrupts the viewing experience and often leads to either wasted data or poor video quality.

💡 Proposed Solution

Implement an intelligent playback system that automatically adjusts video quality based on connection type, battery level, user habits, and device capabilities – while always allowing manual override.

Key Features:

1. Connection-Based Quality Profiles

The player automatically selects optimal quality based on network conditions:

Connection Type Default Quality User Configurable
WiFi Maximum available (1080p/4K) ✅ Yes
Mobile Data (4G/5G) 720p ✅ Yes (can set to 480p, 1080p, etc.)
Roaming 480p (or audio-only) ✅ Yes
Slow Connection Auto-detects and steps down progressively ✅ Threshold configurable
No Connection Switches to downloaded content only N/A

2. Battery-Aware Optimization

· Battery > 30%: Normal quality based on connection.
· Battery 15-30%: Reduce quality one step (e.g., 1080p → 720p).
· Battery < 15% and not charging: Force 480p and suggest audio-only mode.
· Battery < 5% and not charging: Pause background preloading and show warning.
· User override: Option to disable battery-based adjustments.

3. Habit Learning Algorithm

Anizen watches your manual quality adjustments and learns preferences:

User Behavior What Anizen Learns
Always lower quality on AnimeFLV "This source: prefer 480p on mobile"
Always max quality on Crunchyroll "This source: force 1080p even on mobile"
Switch to 720p at night "Late hours: maybe reduce quality"
Never change quality "Stick to defaults"

After 2-3 manual adjustments on the same source/context, Anizen asks:

"I notice you always select 480p when watching on AnimeFLV with mobile data. Would you like me to remember this preference?"

4. Data Usage Dashboard

Real-time stats and history:

Metric Display
Data saved this month "3.2 GB saved thanks to smart quality"
Per-source breakdown "AnimeFLV: 1.1 GB, Crunchyroll: 2.1 GB"
Quality distribution Pie chart: 60% 720p, 30% 1080p, 10% 480p
Projected savings "On track to save 4.5 GB this month"
Data cap alert "You've used 80% of your monthly data"

5. Smart Buffering

· On fast connections: Smaller buffer, faster start.
· On slow connections: Larger buffer to prevent interruptions.
· On mobile data: Buffer size limited to save data.
· Predictive buffering: If you always watch the next episode immediately, pre-buffer it in the background (only on WiFi).

6. Night Mode Integration

· Automatically reduce brightness within the video player during late hours.
· Optional "night quality" profile (e.g., 480p + reduced brightness) to save eyes and battery.
· Time range configurable (e.g., 10 PM – 6 AM).

7. Per-Source Quality Presets

Users can set default quality rules per extension:

```
AnimeFLV:
  - WiFi: 1080p
  - Mobile: 480p (save data)
  - Battery <20%: 360p

Crunchyroll:
  - WiFi: 4K (if available)
  - Mobile: 1080p (always max)
  - Battery: Never reduce
```

8. Manual Override with Memory

· User can change quality at any time during playback.
· After manual change, Anizen asks: "Should I remember this for this source?"
· Option to apply temporarily (just this episode) or permanently.

9. Quality Test on First Play

When a new source is used for the first time:

"Testing optimal quality for your connection..."

· Runs quick speed test.
· Suggests best default quality.
· User can accept or adjust.

10. Offline Quality Selection

When downloading for offline:

· Choose download quality per series: "High (best experience)", "Medium (balanced)", "Low (save space)".
· Automatic recommendation based on device storage.

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

✅ HIGHLY FEASIBLE. CMK did not express any technical objections to this type of feature. The app already has:

· ExoPlayer/MPV integration with quality selection.
· Network connectivity detection.
· Battery level monitoring.
· Per-source settings storage.

What needs to be added:

· Learning algorithm for user habits.
· More granular quality controls.
· Data usage tracking.
· Battery-aware logic.

Complexity Level: Moderate. Most components already exist; this integrates them intelligently.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Foundation

1. Network quality detection:
   ```kotlin
   enum class ConnectionQuality {
       UNKNOWN, POOR, MODERATE, GOOD, EXCELLENT
   }
   ```
   Use ConnectivityManager and bandwidth estimation (e.g., download a small test file or use historical data).
2. Battery monitoring:
   Register BatteryManager broadcasts to track level and charging status.
3. Per-source preferences storage:
   Extend existing Source data class to include quality rules.

Phase 2: Quality Selection Logic

1. Implement QualitySelector class:
   ```kotlin
   fun selectQuality(
       source: Source,
       connectionType: ConnectionType,
       connectionQuality: ConnectionQuality,
       batteryLevel: Int,
       userHabits: UserHabits
   ): VideoQuality
   ```
   This will combine all inputs to choose the optimal quality.
2. Integrate with ExoPlayer:
   Modify track selection logic to use the quality selector before playback starts.

Phase 3: Learning Algorithm

1. Track user overrides:
   Store every manual quality change with context (source, connection, battery, time).
2. Pattern detection:
   After 3+ overrides in similar context, prompt user to save as preference.
3. Habit storage:
   Save learned preferences in a lightweight local database.

Phase 4: UI & Dashboard

1. Data usage tracking:
   · Estimate bytes saved by comparing selected quality vs. maximum.
   · Store daily/weekly/monthly totals.
   · Display in statistics dashboard (integration with Suggestion #1).
2. Settings UI:
   · Per-source quality configuration screen.
   · Global defaults.
   · Battery optimization toggle.
   · Night mode time range.
3. In-player quality indicator:
   · Show current quality and reason (e.g., "720p (mobile data mode)").
   · Quick settings button for manual override.

Phase 5: Advanced Features

1. Speed test on first play:
   · Download small chunk and measure time.
   · Classify connection quality.
   · Suggest optimal default.
2. Predictive buffering:
   · Track episode completion patterns.
   · Preload next episode when likely to binge.

---

📊 Example Scenarios

Scenario Without Feature With Feature
User leaves home (WiFi → mobile) Must manually reduce quality or risk data overage Auto-switches to mobile profile (720p)
Battery at 12%, no charger nearby Video drains remaining battery faster Auto-reduces to 480p, extends playback
User always selects 480p on AnimeFLV with mobile data Repeats manual action daily Learns after 3 times and auto-applies
Traveling abroad (roaming) Forgets to change, returns to huge bill Auto-switches to 480p or warns before playback
Late night viewing Eyes strain from bright screen Auto-dim player, optionally reduce quality

---

🎉 User Benefits

· Never think about quality again: The app handles it intelligently.
· Save data automatically: No more surprise overage charges.
· Extend battery life: Watch more before your phone dies.
· Personalized experience: Learns your preferences over time.
· Full control when wanted: Manual override always available.
· Transparent: Visual indicators and dashboard show what's happening.

---

🎯 Why This Matters

This feature transforms Anizen from a simple video player into an adaptive viewing companion. It respects the user's context (network, battery, habits) and optimizes accordingly without requiring constant attention. Combined with the statistics dashboard (Suggestion #1), users can see exactly how much data and battery they're saving, creating positive reinforcement and deeper engagement with the app.

titulo: 🎯 SUGGESTION #6 FOR ANIZEN: INTEGRATED COMMUNITY HUB
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


---

📉 Current Problem

The Anizen community is scattered across Discord, Telegram, Reddit, and GitHub. Users have to leave the app to ask questions, share discoveries, report broken sources, find recommendations, or see what's new. This fragmentation makes the community feel disconnected, slows down problem-solving, and creates a barrier for new users who don't know where to go for help. Important information (like source outages or new extension updates) doesn't reach users when they need it most.

💡 Proposed Solution

Build an integrated community hub directly inside the Anizen app, turning it from a standalone player into a social ecosystem where users connect, share, and collaborate without ever leaving the app.

Key Features:

1. Community Feed

A scrollable timeline within the app showing:

· Official announcements: New releases, important updates, changelogs (pulled from GitHub).
· Extension updates: Real-time notifications when FelipeGFA or other maintainers update extensions.
· Community posts: Users can share tips, setups, and discoveries (moderated).
· Trending discussions: Popular topics from Discord/GitHub summarized.

2. Crowdsourced Source Health

Real-time status of every extension, powered by the community:

Source Status Reports Last Checked
AnimeFLV 🟢 Working 87 users 2 min ago
Cuevana 🟡 Slow 23 users 5 min ago
FanPelis 🔴 Down 12 users 1 min ago

· Users can report source status with one tap (from Extension Health screen).
· Reports are aggregated and displayed to everyone.
· Historical reliability scores (7-day / 30-day uptime %).

3. Shareable Configuration Codes

· Export your entire Anizen setup (extensions, order, categories, settings) as a compact code or QR.
· Share with friends: "Here's my perfect setup for watching One Piece and Jujutsu Kaisen."
· Import someone else's curated configuration in one tap – perfect for new users.
· Optional: Community library of popular configurations (voted by users).

4. Extension Voting & Requests

· Users can upvote extensions they want prioritized for updates or new features.
· "Most Wanted" list helps developers (like FelipeGFA) know what the community needs.
· Simple interface: Browse extensions, tap 👍, see total votes.

5. In-App Troubleshooting & FAQ

· Built-in knowledge base with solutions to common problems (e.g., "How to fix Cloudflare errors", "Why is my source not loading").
· Community-sourced answers with upvote system.
· Searchable by keywords.
· Option to report a problem directly with logs attached (anonymized).

6. What's New / Changelog

· When Anizen updates, a "What's New" screen appears with:
  · Plain-language summary of changes (not just commit messages).
  · New features highlighted.
  · Fixed bugs listed.
  · Link to full changelog on GitHub.

7. Trending in the Community

· "Popular this week" – shows anime titles that are trending among Anizen users.
· Based on anonymized watch data (opt-in only).
· Helps users discover what others are enjoying.

8. User Profiles (Optional)

· Create a simple profile (optional, privacy-focused).
· Show your watch stats, favorite genres, and shared configurations.
· Follow other users with similar tastes.

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

✅ HIGHLY FEASIBLE. CMK did not express any technical objections to this type of feature. The app already has:

· Network connectivity for fetching data.
· Local storage for preferences.
· Extension metadata.

What needs to be added:

· Integration with GitHub API (for releases, issues, etc.).
· Optional lightweight backend (Firebase or similar) for community features.
· QR code generation/scanning (ZXing library).
· Moderation tools if user-generated content is allowed.

Complexity Level: Moderate. Most features can be implemented with existing Android libraries and minimal backend infrastructure.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Foundation

1. GitHub API integration:
   · Fetch latest releases from Anizen and extension repos.
   · Parse changelogs and display in-app.
2. Extension health reporting:
   · Add "Report Status" button to each extension in Extension Health screen.
   · Store reports locally and optionally sync with a simple backend.

Phase 2: Configuration Sharing

1. Export/import functionality:
   · Serialize user profile (extensions, order, settings) to JSON.
   · Generate QR code using ZXing.
   · Scan QR code and import.
2. Sharing UI:
   · "Share my setup" button in settings.
   · "Import setup" with camera or gallery.

Phase 3: Community Features (Optional Backend)

1. Simple backend (Firebase):
   · Store aggregated health reports (anonymized).
   · Store shared configurations (with user attribution optional).
   · Handle voting counts.
2. Feed implementation:
   · Fetch posts from a curated source (could be a GitHub repo with markdown files).
   · Display with timestamps and categories.

Phase 4: Advanced Features

1. Trending data:
   · Opt-in anonymized watch tracking.
   · Aggregate to show popular titles (privacy-first, no personal data exposed).
2. User profiles:
   · Optional account system (email/password or OAuth).
   · Profile customization.

---

⚠️ Privacy Considerations

Feature Privacy Approach
Source health reports Anonymous, no user identification
Configuration sharing User chooses what to share; no personal data required
Trending Aggregated, anonymized, opt-in
User profiles Optional, with clear privacy policy
In-app feedback Can include anonymized logs with user consent

---

🎉 User Benefits

· One-stop shop: Everything community-related inside the app.
· Faster problem solving: See if a source is down for everyone or just you.
· Easy setup: Import perfect configurations from experienced users.
· Influence development: Vote on what matters to you.
· Discover new anime: See what others are watching.
· Never miss updates: Changelog and announcements right in your face.

---

🎯 Why This Matters

This feature transforms Anizen from a solo experience into a community-driven platform. It creates a virtuous cycle: users help each other, developers see real feedback, and the app improves faster. The community hub becomes the reason users stay – not just for the anime, but for the connection with fellow fans.

titulo: 🎯 SPECIAL SUGGESTION FOR ANIZEN: ULTIMATE HIGH-PERFORMANCE CONFIGURATION MODE
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature



For users who want absolute control over every aspect of performance, battery, and rendering – because sometimes "auto" just isn't enough 🚀⚡

---

📉 Current Problem

Anizen currently offers a basic "disable animations" option, but power users – especially those with older devices, specific performance needs, or who use Anizen for extended periods – have no way to fine‑tune the app's behavior at a system level. They face issues like:

· Thermal throttling during long binge sessions.
· Battery drain when they need maximum playback time.
· Stuttering or lag on devices with limited GPU capabilities.
· Wi-Fi instability when the screen is off, causing buffering.
· Inconsistent frame rates due to lack of GPU configuration.

There's no single place to control rendering, networking, and power management in a unified, expert‑friendly way.

---

💡 Proposed Solution

Add an Ultimate High‑Performance Configuration Mode – a dedicated settings panel (hidden behind an "Expert" toggle) that gives users granular control over:

· Graphics rendering (OpenGL / Vulkan)
· Anti‑aliasing (MSAA)
· Resolution scaling
· Texture management
· Wi‑Fi behavior during screen off
· CPU wake locks
· Screen brightness/dimming behavior

This would be optional, off by default, and clearly marked as "for advanced users only" to prevent accidental misconfiguration.

---

⚙️ DETAILED CONFIGURATION OPTIONS

1. Graphics Rendering Engine

Choose the underlying graphics API for video playback and UI rendering:

Option Description
Auto Let the system decide (default)
OpenGL Force OpenGL ES rendering (compatibility, widely supported)
Vulkan Force Vulkan rendering (better performance on modern devices, lower CPU overhead)
Game Engine Mode Experimental: use game‑optimized rendering pipeline (if applicable)

Why: Vulkan can significantly reduce CPU load and improve frame pacing on devices that support it, leading to smoother playback and less battery drain.

---

2. Anti‑Aliasing (MSAA)

Option Description
Off No anti‑aliasing (maximum performance)
2x Basic edge smoothing
4x Good balance
8x High quality
16x Maximum quality (if supported)

Plus toggles:

· Apply MSAA to framebuffers – extends anti‑aliasing to off‑screen buffers for even smoother graphics (may impact performance).

Why: Reduces jagged edges in UI and video scaling, but at a performance cost. Power users can choose their preferred trade‑off.

---

3. Resolution Scaling

Control the resolution at which the app renders:

Option Description
Native Use device's native resolution (best quality)
Quality Slightly downscaled for smoother performance
Performance Aggressive downscaling for maximum speed
Custom (unsafe) Manually set width/height (warning: may cause visual artifacts)

Resolution change method:

· Advanced – for correct shadows and UI scaling (recommended)
· Compatibility – fallback for problematic devices

Why: Lower resolution = higher performance. Essential for devices struggling with 1080p/4K playback.

---

4. Texture Management

Fine‑tune how textures are loaded and compressed:

Option Choices
Texture size Smaller textures (performance) / Normal (quality)
Texture decompression All (compatibility) / Memory‑optimized
Texture compression Decompressed only / Use hardware compression

Why: Textures consume memory and bandwidth. Reducing their size or using compression can free up RAM for smoother playback.

---

5. Wi‑Fi Behavior During Screen Off

Control how Wi‑Fi behaves when the device is idle or the screen is off – critical for uninterrupted streaming during long listening/watching sessions.

Option Description
Wi‑Fi scan‑only When screen off, Wi‑Fi stays active but only scans (minimal battery, may cause buffering)
Wi‑Fi normal Normal behavior (system default)
Wi‑Fi high performance Keep Wi‑Fi in high‑performance mode even with screen off (prevents disconnects, uses more battery)

Why: On many devices, Wi‑Fi drops to low‑power mode when the screen is off, causing buffering during background audio or long playback. High‑performance mode prevents this.

---

6. CPU Wake Locks (Power Management)

Control whether the CPU stays awake in various scenarios – essential for devices that have trouble waking from sleep or for uninterrupted playback.

Option Behavior
Processor (full wake lock) Keeps CPU awake even if power button pressed or display times out. Fixes "device won't wake up" issues.
Screen dimmed Screen stays on, but can dim. Power button releases lock.
Screen bright Screen at full brightness always. Power button releases lock.
Screen and Keyboard Keep display and (if applicable) keyboard at full brightness.

Why: Some devices (e.g., Galaxy Note 4) have well‑known wake‑up issues. This gives users the tools to work around them.

---

7. Additional Performance Tweaks

· 16‑bit colors – use 16‑bit instead of 32‑bit for UI rendering (saves memory, may reduce visual quality)
· Force disable Vulkan – emergency override if Vulkan causes issues
· Enable settings for this app – master toggle for all performance overrides

---

8. Profiles (Quick Presets)

To make this powerful panel accessible, include quick‑apply profiles:

Profile Description
Battery Saver Low resolution, textures small, Wi‑Fi scan‑only, no MSAA
Balanced Medium settings, auto engine, Wi‑Fi normal
Performance Native resolution, Vulkan (if available), MSAA 4x, Wi‑Fi high performance, full wake locks
Custom User‑defined settings

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

⚠️ POSSIBLE BUT COMPLEX. CMK hasn't directly addressed this, but we can infer:

· Graphics settings (OpenGL/Vulkan, MSAA) may require changes to the underlying video player (ExoPlayer/MPV) or Compose rendering layer.
· Wi‑Fi behavior can be controlled via WifiManager and PowerManager APIs (requires appropriate permissions).
· Wake locks are standard Android PowerManager features – feasible but need careful handling to avoid battery drain.
· Resolution scaling is possible via Surface scaling or by manipulating Display metrics.

What's already there:

· Anizen uses modern Android APIs that can be extended.
· Permissions for wake locks and Wi‑Fi control are available (user must grant).

What needs to be added:

· UI for all these controls (potentially large settings screen).
· Integration with video player to apply graphics settings.
· Proper handling of edge cases (e.g., device doesn't support Vulkan).
· Safety warnings and disclaimers.

Complexity Level: High – this touches many system areas, but it's all doable with Android's public APIs.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Foundation

1. Create new settings screen: "Ultimate Performance" under Settings → Advanced.
2. Add master toggle: "Enable advanced performance controls" (off by default).
3. Store preferences in DataStore with sensible defaults.

Phase 2: Graphics Controls

1. Integrate with ExoPlayer/MPV: Pass rendering engine preference (OpenGL/Vulkan) via player configuration.
2. Implement MSAA: This may require changes to the SurfaceView/TextureView rendering chain – research needed.
3. Resolution scaling: Manipulate View dimensions or use DisplayMetrics to scale content.

Phase 3: Wi‑Fi & Power

1. Wi‑Fi controls: Use WifiManager and ConnectivityManager to adjust Wi‑Fi policies. Note: some behaviors may require CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (for scan‑only mode).
2. Wake locks: Implement using PowerManager with appropriate flags. Show clear warning about battery impact.
3. Screen dim/bright controls: Use WindowManager.LayoutParams flags.

Phase 4: Profiles

1. Profile system: Save/load groups of settings. Provide quick‑apply buttons.

Phase 5: Safety & Testing

1. Compatibility checks: Detect device capabilities (Vulkan support, MSAA levels) and hide unavailable options.
2. Warnings: Add bold disclaimers: "These settings can affect battery life and stability. Use at your own risk."
3. Reset to defaults button: One‑tap to restore safe settings.

---

⚠️ Potential Concerns & Solutions

Concern Solution
Battery drain Warn users; default to off; provide "Battery Saver" profile
Instability Extensive testing on various devices; option to reset to defaults
User confusion Hide behind "Expert" toggle; use clear language; tooltips
Permissions Request at runtime when user enables specific features
Vulkan not supported Automatically hide option or show "not available"

---

🎉 User Benefits

· Ultimate control: Tune every aspect of the app to match your device and needs.
· Fix device‑specific issues: Wake locks can resolve sleep‑of‑death problems.
· Maximize performance: Get the smoothest playback on low‑end devices.
· Extend battery life: Aggressive power saving when needed.
· Professional‑grade: Appeals to power users and enthusiasts.

---

🎯 Why This Matters

Anizen already appeals to a wide audience, but power users are the ones who evangelize, contribute, and stick around. Giving them this level of control shows that Anizen respects their expertise and needs. It's the difference between a good app and a great one that users become passionate about.

---

🏷️ Hashtags

#Anizen #FeatureRequest #UltimatePerformance #PowerUsers #Vulkan #OpenGL #WakeLock #WiFiOptimization #AdvancedSettings

---

🫡 MESSAGE TO CMK

"CMK, this one's for the power users – the ones who stay up late tweaking settings, who know what Vulkan is, who have older devices they refuse to give up. This feature would make Anizen the go‑to app for anyone who wants absolute control over their anime experience.

Yes, it's complex. Yes, it's probably low priority. But it's the kind of feature that builds a cult following. People will recommend Anizen just because 'you can tweak EVERYTHING'.

If you ever decide to tackle this, start small: maybe just the Wi‑Fi and wake lock controls first, then graphics. And always, always put up warning signs so casual users don't wander in.

Thanks for considering, and for everything you've already built." 🔥

---

Pd: If this is too crazy, even a simplified version with just Wi‑Fi high‑performance and basic CPU wake locks would be a huge win for users with connectivity issues. Just saying. 😉

titulo: 🎯 SUGGESTION #7 FOR ANIZEN: EXPERT MODE – AUTOMATION & SCRIPTING (IFTTT STYLE)
body_original:
### Describe your suggested feature


Plus a Special Bonus Recommendation: Ultimate High‑Performance Configuration Mode 🚀⚡

---

📉 Current Problem

Advanced users want to customize Anizen beyond what the interface offers. They have repetitive tasks that currently require manual intervention: switching sources when one fails, downloading new episodes automatically, organizing their library in specific ways, cleaning up old content, and managing multiple series with complex rules. There's no way to automate these workflows, forcing power users to do everything manually or switch between multiple apps. This limits Anizen's potential for users who want a truly personalized, hands-off experience.

Additionally, power users with specific device needs – older hardware, thermal constraints, or unique performance requirements – have no way to fine‑tune the app's behavior at a system level. Issues like Wi‑Fi dropping during screen‑off, GPU rendering glitches, or excessive battery drain during long sessions remain unaddressed.

---

💡 Proposed Solution

Introduce an Expert Mode with two complementary subsystems:

1. Automation Engine – IFTTT‑style rules for workflow automation.
2. Ultimate High‑Performance Configuration – granular control over rendering, networking, and power management.

Both are optional, off by default, and clearly marked as "for advanced users only" to prevent accidental misconfiguration.

---

🤖 PART 1: AUTOMATION ENGINE (IFTTT STYLE)

Key Features

1. Rule‑Based Automation Engine

Users can create custom automation rules with an easy, beginner‑friendly interface:

Trigger (IF) Condition Action (THEN)
New episode available Of specific series Download automatically
Source health changes 🔴 Critical for >2 hours Migrate all titles to backup source
Time/day Sunday 8 PM Show recommendations for short anime (<20 eps)
Series completed Any Add next season to "Plan to Watch"
Storage space Below 1GB Delete oldest watched episodes
WiFi connection Connected Pre‑download next 3 episodes of active series
Battery level Below 15% Reduce streaming quality to 480p
New series added Genre = shonen Add to "Shonen" category
User activity No activity for 7 days Send notification: "You have 5 unwatched episodes"

2. Comprehensive Trigger Library

Trigger Category Examples
Content triggers New episode available, series completed, new season detected, source updated
Source health triggers Source status changes (🟢→🔴, 🔴→🟢), latency threshold crossed, source down for X minutes
Time triggers Specific time/day, sunset/sunrise, after X hours of inactivity, weekly schedule
Connection triggers WiFi connected/disconnected, mobile data detected, roaming, no connection
Device triggers Battery level threshold, storage space low/high, charging starts/stops, device boot
Library triggers New series added, episode marked watched, series marked completed/dropped, category changed
User activity triggers Idle for X days, binge session detected, watch streak reached

3. Extensive Action Library

Action Category Examples
Download actions Download episode (with quality preference), prioritize series in queue, batch download
Source actions Change source for specific titles, test source health, refresh source data, migrate all from dead source
Library actions Move series to category, mark as read/unread, update status, add tags
Cleanup actions Delete watched episodes older than X days, clear cache, compress downloaded media
Notification actions Send push notification, show in‑app alert, send email (optional)
Tracking actions Update MAL/AniList/MyAnimeList, sync progress
Backup actions Export library backup, sync to cloud (from Suggestion #3)
Playback actions Change quality profile, switch to audio‑only, enable night mode
Integration actions Export to third‑party apps, share list

4. Advanced Conditional Logic

Complexity Example
AND IF new episode AND source latency < 2 seconds AND WiFi connected THEN download immediately
OR IF source is down OR latency > 5 seconds for 10 minutes THEN switch to backup
Nested IF (storage < 2GB AND chapters older than 30 days exist) THEN delete oldest 100 chapters
Counters IF failed downloads > 3 in 1 hour THEN pause downloads and notify
Priorities High priority: always download One Piece episodes immediately

5. Shareable Automation Recipes

· Export your automation rules as a shareable code/snippet.
· Community hub (Suggestion #6) becomes a marketplace of automation ideas.
· One‑click import of popular recipes from other users.
· Rating and commenting on recipes.

6. Execution Logs & Monitoring

```
[Today 2:00 AM] Rule #1 triggered: Downloaded 3 episodes of One Piece
[Today 2:05 AM] Rule #4 triggered: Migrated 8 titles from AnimeFLV to Jkanime
[Today 3:00 AM] Rule #7 triggered: Cleaned up 150 old chapters, freed 450MB
```

7. Dry Run / Simulation Mode

"Dry run complete: 12 episodes would be downloaded, 8 series would be migrated, 450MB would be freed."

8. Rule Priority System

Assign priority levels; if multiple rules conflict, higher priority wins.

9. Scheduled Rule Execution

Run rules at specific times, on device boot, or when conditions are met.

10. Integration with All Previous Suggestions

· With Statistics: "IF reading streak > 7 days, show congratulatory message."
· With Offline Mode: "IF offline mode activated, auto‑show downloaded content."
· With Cloud Sync: "IF backup older than 7 days, auto‑backup to cloud."
· With Smart Library: "IF new genre detected, create category."
· With Smart Playback: "IF battery < 20%, reduce quality."
· With Community Hub: "IF source reported down by 10+ users, auto‑migrate."

---

⚙️ PART 2: SPECIAL BONUS RECOMMENDATION – ULTIMATE HIGH‑PERFORMANCE CONFIGURATION MODE

For users who need absolute control over rendering, networking, and power management

Why This Matters

Some users face device‑specific issues: Wi‑Fi dropping during screen‑off, GPU glitches, excessive battery drain, or thermal throttling. A basic "disable animations" toggle isn't enough.

Proposed Configuration Options

1. Graphics Rendering Engine

Option Description
Auto System default
OpenGL Force OpenGL ES (maximum compatibility)
Vulkan Force Vulkan (lower CPU overhead, smoother on modern devices)
Game Engine Mode Experimental rendering pipeline

2. Anti‑Aliasing (MSAA)

Option Description
Off / 2x / 4x / 8x / 16x Smooth jagged edges at a performance cost
Apply MSAA to framebuffers Extend anti‑aliasing to off‑screen buffers

3. Resolution Scaling

Option Description
Native Device's native resolution
Quality Slight downscale for smoother performance
Performance Aggressive downscale for maximum speed
Custom (unsafe) Manual width/height input (warning)

Resolution change method: Advanced (for correct shadows) / Compatibility

4. Texture Management

Option Choices
Texture size Smaller textures (performance) / Normal (quality)
Texture decompression All (compatibility) / Memory‑optimized
Texture compression Decompressed only / Hardware compression

5. Wi‑Fi Behavior During Screen Off

Option Description
Wi‑Fi scan‑only Minimal battery, may cause buffering
Wi‑Fi normal System default
Wi‑Fi high performance Keep Wi‑Fi active even with screen off (prevents disconnects)

6. CPU Wake Locks (Power Management)

Option Behavior
Processor (full wake lock) CPU stays awake even if screen off; fixes wake‑up issues
Screen dimmed Screen stays on, can dim; power button releases lock
Screen bright Screen at full brightness always
Screen and Keyboard Keep display and keyboard at full brightness

7. Additional Tweaks

· 16‑bit colors – use 16‑bit instead of 32‑bit for UI (saves memory)
· Force disable Vulkan – emergency override
· Enable settings for this app – master toggle for all performance overrides

8. Quick Preset Profiles

Profile Description
Battery Saver Low resolution, small textures, Wi‑Fi scan‑only, no MSAA
Balanced Medium settings, auto engine, Wi‑Fi normal
Performance Native resolution, Vulkan (if available), MSAA 4x, Wi‑Fi high performance, full wake locks
Custom User‑defined

---

🔧 Technical Feasibility (Based on CMK's Feedback)

⚠️ COMPLEX BUT POSSIBLE. CMK's comments guide us:

· "I can do that if it actually feels right" – Features must feel natural, not overwhelming.
· "The app needs breathing space" – Background processing must be respectful.
· "You know I am not a genius" – Humility, but not an admission of impossibility.

What's already there:

· All data needed for automation (episode status, source health, etc.)
· All actions (downloads, migrations) exist as manual functions
· Local database for rules and logs
· Modern Android APIs for graphics, Wi‑Fi, and power management

What needs to be added:

· Rule parser and execution engine
· Background worker for condition checks
· UI for rule creation and management
· Graphics settings integration with ExoPlayer/MPV
· Wi‑Fi and wake lock controls with proper permissions
· Safety disclaimers and compatibility checks

Complexity Level: High – but achievable with a phased approach.

---

📋 Suggested Implementation Steps

Phase 1: Automation Foundation

1. Database schema for rules and logs
2. Basic rule engine (time‑based, connection‑based)
3. Simple form‑based rule builder UI

Phase 2: Expand Automation

1. Add content, source health, and device triggers
2. Expand actions (downloads, source changes, notifications)
3. Add conditional logic (AND/OR)

Phase 3: Performance Configuration

1. Graphics engine selection and MSAA controls
2. Resolution scaling and texture management
3. Wi‑Fi behavior controls
4. Wake lock implementation

Phase 4: Advanced Automation

1. Rule priorities and conflict resolution
2. Dry run mode
3. Recipe sharing and import

Phase 5: Polish & Integration

1. Execution logs UI
2. Quick preset profiles
3. Integration with Community Hub (Suggestion #6)

---

⚠️ Potential Concerns & Solutions

Concern Solution
Battery drain Use WorkManager with constraints; warn users
Complexity Hide behind "Expert" toggle; provide templates
Rule conflicts Clear priority system and resolution UI
Instability Compatibility checks; reset to defaults button
Permissions Request at runtime when features are enabled

---

🎉 User Benefits

· Total personalization: Anizen adapts to YOUR workflow and device.
· Save hours of manual work: Automation handles repetitive tasks.
· Fix device‑specific issues: Wake locks and Wi‑Fi controls solve real problems.
· Maximize performance: Tune every aspect for your hardware.
· Shareable intelligence: Learn from the community's best automations.
· Never miss content: Auto‑download ensures you always have something to watch.

---

🎯 Why This Matters

These two features together transform Anizen from an excellent anime app into a platform for power users. Automation handles the "what" (workflow), while performance configuration handles the "how" (system behavior). No other anime app offers this level of customization.

This is what builds a cult following – users who recommend Anizen not just because it works, but because they can make it work exactly how they want.

---

📊 Example Complete Power User Scenario

Rule Trigger Condition Action
1 Friday 6 PM WiFi connected Download next 5 episodes of all active series
2 Source health AnimeFLV down >1 hour Migrate all AnimeFLV titles to Jkanime
3 Battery <20% and not charging Reduce streaming quality to 480p
4 Storage <1GB free Delete oldest 50 watched episodes
5 New episode Of "One Piece" Download immediately (priority high)

Plus Performance Settings:

· Vulkan rendering (if supported)
· Wi‑Fi high performance mode
· Processor wake lock enabled
· MSAA 4x for smoother UI

All of this happens automatically. User just opens the app and watches.

---

🏷️ Hashtags

#Anizen #FeatureRequest #ExpertMode #Automation #IFTTT #PowerUsers #PerformanceMode #Vulkan #WakeLock #GameChanger

---

🫡 FINAL MESSAGE TO CMK

### Describe why this should be added

```markdown

**Target Repository:**
- `yuzono/anime-extensions`

---

## 0. Executive Summary

This document defines an **eight-phase (0 to 7)** development plan to transform `yuzono/anime-extensions` into a coherent, maintainable, and well-documented catalog of anime sources for the Aniyomi/Miyomi ecosystem.

- **Phase 0 – Audit & Sanitation:** Inventory, classify, detect breaks, duplicates, and gaps.
- **Phase 1 – Technical Standardization:** Establish internal rules, shared helpers, and quality criteria.
- **Phase 2 – Coverage & Prioritization:** Decide which anime sources are core, experimental, or belong to cursed.
- **Phase 3 – Documentation & Discovery:** README, wiki, metadata, and usage guides.
- **Phase 4 – Governance & Contributions:** Contribution rules, templates, and clear roles.
- **Phase 5 – Automation & Health:** Periodic checks, metrics, and health monitoring.
- **Phase 6 – Consolidation & Scale:** Controlled expansion, debt reduction, and refinement.
- **Phase 7 – Maintenance, Archive & Cycle Closure:** Deprecation, archiving, lessons learned.

**Core principle:** Observe first (Phase 0), normalize (Phase 1), prioritize (Phase 2), then make it sustainable through documentation, rules, and automation.

---

## 1. Context & Purpose

### 1.1 Repository

- `yuzono/anime-extensions` – Anime extension catalog for Aniyomi ecosystem.

### 1.2 Alignment with Community Rules

This plan operates within the following community guidelines:

1. **Respect & Consideration** – All contributors and users are treated with respect regardless of background.
2. **No Personal Attacks** – Disagreements are resolved civilly and privately.
3. **Privacy** – No personal information is shared without consent.
4. **No Spam** – Repetitive messages and unauthorized ads are prohibited.
5. **Support Channels** – Support requests go to designated support channels, not general chat.
6. **No Source Recommendations** – This plan does **not** recommend sources to end users. It is a technical maintenance document for contributors. Third-party repositories are not affiliated and are not supported.
7. **No Repeated Fix Requests** – Known issues are addressed when contributors have time. Repeated requests are discouraged.

### 1.3 Problems to Solve

- Broken anime extensions without clear status or tracking.
- Duplicates between repositories (same source in anime and cursed repos) without clear criteria.
- Inconsistent technical conventions: naming, structure, helpers.
- Insufficient documentation: users and contributors are confused.
- Reactive maintenance without priorities or metrics.

### 1.4 Overall Goals

1. **Visibility:** Know which anime extensions exist, what they do, and their status.
2. **Consistency:** Similar extensions follow similar technical patterns.
3. **Priority:** Effort goes first to what provides the most value to the community.
4. **Traceability:** Every important decision leaves a trace (issue, changelog, wiki).
5. **Sustainability:** The ecosystem doesn't depend on ad-hoc memory but on simple rules.

---

## 2. Design Principles

1. **Observe first, then act** – No blind refactoring; audit first.
2. **Core before periphery** – Most used and critical extensions come first.
3. **Minimum viable standardization** – Small, clear, mandatory standards, not an impossible bible.
4. **Experimental ≠ chaotic** – Cursed sources can be more flexible, but not opaque.
5. **Every important change leaves a trace** – Issue, labeled PR, changelog entry, or wiki note.
6. **Automation supports judgment, doesn't replace it** – Scripts detect breaks and states; humans decide actions.

---

## 3. Phase 0 – Audit & Sanitation

### 3.1 Objective

Build an honest and complete picture of the actual state of all anime extensions in the repository.

### 3.2 Scope

- All extensions from `yuzono/anime-extensions`.

### 3.3 Deliverables

- **Inventory** – Table with one row per extension.
- **Status classification** per extension:
  - Stable, partially broken, broken, experimental, cursed.
- **List of broken extensions.**
- **Duplicate map** between anime and cursed repos.
- **Gap list** (requested anime sources with no extension or poor state).
- **Audit criteria document** – How each status was determined.

### 3.4 Inventory Table Model

```markdown
| Name       | Language | Region  | Type   | Domain              | Status | Priority | Maintenance | Notes                          |
|------------|----------|---------|--------|---------------------|--------|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| AnimeSama  | FR       | France  | Anime  | https://animesama.fr| 🟢     | High     | Active      | Frequent domain changes        |
| Vostfree   | FR       | France  | Anime  | https://vostfree.com| 🟡     | Medium   | Weak        | Occasional catalog errors      |
| AnimeVostFr| FR       | Global  | Anime  | https://animevost.fr| 🧿     | Low      | Volatile    | Aggressive Cloudflare bypass   |
```

3.5 Status Criteria

· 🟢 Stable – Installs without error; lists catalog; allows streaming; handles errors without breaking experience.
· 🟡 Partially Broken – Some critical functions fail (search, certain series, etc.); usable but with visible issues.
· 🔴 Broken – Doesn't install, list content, or allow streaming; critical errors constant.
· 🧪 Experimental – Frequent structural changes; works but no stability guarantee.
· 🧿 Cursed – Unusual behavior, extreme fragility, or aggressive bypasses; recognized as useful but not suitable as stable core.

3.6 Mini-Test Checklist per Extension

1. Install the extension in the target client (Aniyomi, etc.).
2. Open the catalog – Does it load titles?
3. Search for a known title – Does it appear?
4. Open details and episode – Does content display?
5. Observe unusual redirects, captchas, or blocks.

This checklist consistently assigns 🟢/🟡/🔴/🧪/🧿 status.

3.7 Recommended Phase 0 Issues

· [F0][CORE] Initial extension inventory – anime-extensions
· [F0][CORE] Catalog of broken anime extensions
· [F0][CORE] Definition of health statuses (🟢/🟡/🔴/🧪/🧿)
· [F0][CORE] Anime/cursed duplicates and resolution proposal

---

4. Phase 1 – Technical Standardization

4.1 Objective

Reduce unnecessary technical variability and establish a minimum internal standard that all anime extensions must follow.

4.2 Deliverables

· STANDARD_TECH.md file in the organization or repo.
· Shared helpers module.
· Naming convention for packages and classes.
· Versioning convention.
· Minimum quality checklist.
· Examples of "well-made" anime extensions.

4.3 Suggested STANDARD_TECH.md Content

```markdown
# STANDARD_TECH.md – Anime

## Objective

Define how anime extensions in the ecosystem should be structured, documented, and maintained.

## Basic Rules

- Mandatory naming conventions.
- Shared helpers for repetitive logic.
- Uniform error handling.
- Consistent versioning.
- Minimum documentation per extension.

## Source Classification

- Core: Stable and maintained.
- Experimental: Frequent changes or moderate risk.
- Cursed: Fragile, non-standard, or special maintenance source.

## Minimum Quality Criteria

- Installs correctly.
- Lists catalog.
- Opens content.
- Reports errors clearly.

## Review

This document is reviewed after each audit cycle or major ecosystem changes.
```

4.4 Pillar 1: Naming & Structure Conventions

· Consistent package names across repositories (e.g., eu.yuzono.anime.lang.region.SourceName).
· Folder per language/region.
· Source classes with coherent suffixes (AnimeSource, etc.).

4.5 Pillar 2: Shared Helpers

· Common modules for:
  · Headers and user-agent.
  · Cookies and sessions.
  · Anti-bot and Cloudflare handling.
  · Repetitive parsing (episode lists, video URLs, etc.).

4.6 Pillar 3: Error Handling

· Common pattern for HTTP errors (404, 500, timeouts).
· Clear user messages: "Source X is temporarily unavailable", etc.
· Treat anti-bot blocks as detectable and documented states.

4.7 Pillar 4: Versioning & Changes

· Version scheme (e.g., SemVer adapted: major.minor.patch).
· Changelog for functional changes and breaking changes.
· Don't mix internal refactors with behavior changes without annotation.

4.8 Pillar 5: Minimum Quality

· Mandatory:
  · Installation without error.
  · Functional catalog.
  · Reproducible streaming.
  · Visible and understandable errors.

4.9 Recommended Phase 1 Issues

· [F1][CORE] Minimum technical standard document (STANDARD_TECH.md) – Anime
· [F1][CORE] Shared helpers for headers/UA/cookies/anti-bot – Anime
· [F1][CORE] Unified package and versioning convention – Anime
· [F1][ANIME] Refactor 5 core anime extensions

---

5. Phase 2 – Coverage & Prioritization

5.1 Objective

Explicitly decide which anime sources are core (priority), which are experimental, and which belong to the cursed space.

5.2 Deliverables

· List of core anime sources.
· Coverage matrix by language, region, and type.
· Classification of official / unofficial / experimental sources.
· Map of relevant gaps.

5.3 Criteria for Core Anime Sources

· Relevant and recurring usage by the community.
· Reasonable stability.
· Clear value: large library, good content quality.
· Active maintainer or community willing to maintain.

5.4 Coverage Matrix (Example)

```markdown
| Language | Region     | Type   | Core Anime? | Cursed? | Notes                         |
|----------|------------|--------|-------------|---------|-------------------------------|
| FR       | France     | Anime  | Yes         | No      | Main VOSTFR sources           |
| EN       | Global     | Anime  | Yes         | No      | Major simulcast sources       |
| RU       | Russia     | Anime  | No          | Yes     | Volatile sources              |
| ES       | Spain      | Anime  | No          | No      | Growing demand                 |
```

5.5 Recommended Phase 2 Issues

· [F2][CORE] Define essential anime sources per language/region
· [F2][CORE] Coverage matrix (language, type, region) – Anime
· [F2][CORE] Gap analysis vs other catalogs (Keiyoushi, etc.) – Anime
· [F2][ANIME] Prioritization of most requested anime sources
· [F2][CURSED] Definition of cursed anime sources and limits

---

6. Phase 3 – Documentation & Discovery

6.1 Objective

Enable users and contributors to understand the anime extension ecosystem without relying on oral explanations or digging through code.

6.2 Deliverables

· Main README updated (English + optionally other languages).
· Wiki with:
  · Repository installation guide.
  · Basic usage guide.
  · Core anime extension lists.
  · Technical FAQ.
· Minimum metadata per extension (in table or cards).
· Migration guide between repos (e.g., anime ↔ cursed).

6.3 Minimum README Content

· What is the Yūzōnō anime extension ecosystem.
· How to add the repo to Aniyomi.
· What core, experimental, and cursed mean for anime sources.
· Where to report issues and where to see extension status.

6.4 Metadata per Extension (Example Card)

```markdown
## AnimeSamaFR

- Language: FR
- Region: France
- Type: Anime (VOSTFR streaming)
- Status: 🟢 Stable
- Classification: Core
- Special dependencies: Moderate Cloudflare
- Notes: Check domain changes every X months.
```

6.5 Recommended Phase 3 Issues

· [F3][DOCS] Main README review and rewrite – Anime
· [F3][DOCS] Roadmap wiki and usage guide – Anime
· [F3][DOCS] Metadata cards for core anime extensions
· [F3][DOCS] Migration guide (anime ↔ cursed)

---

7. Phase 4 – Governance & Contributions

7.1 Objective

Prevent the project from relying solely on implicit decisions; provide clear rules for contributing and maintaining.

7.2 Deliverables

· CONTRIBUTING.md with:
  · Style rules.
  · Requirements for new anime sources.
  · Review process.
· Issue and PR templates in .github/.
· Role definitions:
  · Primary maintainer.
  · Co-maintainers.
  · Technical reviewers.
  · Documentation owners.
· Acceptance, deprecation, and removal policies.

7.3 Suggested Contribution Rules

· Every PR must indicate if it:
  · Adds an anime source.
  · Fixes an anime source.
  · Refactors structure.
  · Deprecates or removes something.
· Every new anime source must declare:
  · Language.
  · Region.
  · Type.
  · Initial status (stable/experimental/cursed).
· Cursed anime sources must be explicitly labeled and explain why they are considered cursed.

7.4 Key Policies

· New source acceptance policy:
  · Assess need, potential stability, and future cost.
  · Prioritize high-value real sources.
· Deprecation and removal policy:
  · Mark as deprecated before removal.
  · Note the reason (irreparable break, abandonment, conflicts, etc.).
  · Suggest alternatives if available.

7.5 Recommended Phase 4 Issues

· [F4][CORE/DOCS] Issue and PR templates – Anime
· [F4][DOCS] CONTRIBUTING.md – Anime
· [F4][CORE] New anime source acceptance policy
· [F4][CORE] Deprecation and removal policy – Anime

---

8. Phase 5 – Automation & Ecosystem Health

8.1 Objective

Reduce repetitive manual work and have early signals of breaks or degradation in anime extensions.

8.2 Deliverables

· Scripts or checking tools.
· Health check checklist.
· Basic state metrics.
· Periodic review pattern.

8.3 Possible Automations

· Periodic base URL checks (do they respond?).
· Critical selector verification (do they return reasonable episode data?).
· Detection of extensions with no recent commits or changes.
· Generation of textual health report.

8.4 Minimum Metrics

· Total number of active anime extensions.
· Number of broken extensions (🔴).
· Number of partially broken extensions (🟡).
· Number of experimental extensions (🧪).
· Number of cursed extensions (🧿).
· Average time to resolve critical issues.

8.5 Recommended Phase 5 Issues

· [F5][CORE] Periodic core anime source health check script
· [F5][CORE] Textual repo health dashboard – Anime
· [F5][CORE] Periodic review policy (monthly/quarterly) – Anime
· [F5][DOCS] Metrics and ecosystem state log – Anime

---

9. Phase 6 – Consolidation & Scale

9.1 Objective

Consolidate what was achieved in previous phases and scale the anime extension ecosystem without losing control.

9.2 Deliverables

· Batch expansion plan for anime extensions.
· Consolidation of helpers and repeated patterns.
· Duplicate reduction.
· Identified and partially resolved technical debt.

9.3 Activities

· Review which core anime extensions meet the technical standard.
· Homogenize those that don't.
· Absorb duplicates (merge or remove redundancies).
· Promote mature extensions (experimental → core).
· Retire or archive extensions that no longer provide value.

9.4 Success Criteria

· Less code duplication.
· More consistency between extensions.
· Less maintenance time per extension.
· Sufficient documentation for newcomers to contribute.

9.5 Recommended Phase 6 Issues

· [F6][CORE] Common helpers consolidation – Anime
· [F6][CORE] Cross-repo duplicate cleanup – Anime
· [F6][CORE] Mature anime source promotion to core
· [F6][CORE] Technical debt reduction from Phase 0 – Anime

---

10. Phase 7 – Maintenance, Archive & Cycle Closure

10.1 Objective

Close the lifecycle of anime extensions and the plan itself without leaving noise or invisible decisions.

10.2 Deliverables

· Archive and legacy state policy.
· Historical record of key decisions.
· Lessons learned document.
· Updated roadmap for the next cycle.

10.3 Actions

· Move obsolete extensions to legacy status or archive them.
· Remove irreparable anime sources or those that no longer make sense.
· Preserve useful history in the wiki or log files.
· Document reasons for removal or freezing.
· Adjust the plan for the next cycle based on learnings.

10.4 Cycle Closure Criteria

· A user can clearly distinguish active from obsolete.
· A maintainer can justify what's alive and what's archived.
· The repo doesn't accumulate unexplained noise.

10.5 Recommended Phase 7 Issues

· [F7][CORE] Archive and legacy state policy – Anime
· [F7][CORE] Historical record of major decisions and changes – Anime
· [F7][DOCS] Lessons learned from the cycle (postmortem) – Anime
· [F7][CORE] Final cleanup of obsolete anime extensions

---


### Other details

11. Appendix A – Detailed Inventory Structure

```markdown
| Name | Language | Region | Type | Domain | Status | Priority | Maintenance | Notes |
|------|----------|--------|------|--------|--------|----------|-------------|-------|
```

Recommended Fields:

· Name: Human-readable extension name.
· Language: Main language of the source.
· Region: Geographic focus.
· Type: Anime, etc.
· Domain: Base URL.
· Status: 🟢/🟡/🔴/🧪/🧿.
· Priority: High/Medium/Low.
· Maintenance: Active/Weak/Abandoned.
· Notes: Technical or operational observations.

---

12. Appendix B – General Issue Template (Anime)

```markdown
### Title

[Fx][AREA] Brief task description – Anime

### Objective

Explain what you want to achieve and why.

### Scope

Affected anime sources, approximate number of changes.

### Details

- Suggested steps
- Acceptance criteria
- Known risks

### Expected Outcome

What should be different after completing the issue.
```

---

13. Appendix C – Decision on "Cursed" (Anime)

An anime extension is considered cursed when:

· Requires exceptional maintenance due to extreme fragility.
· Changes domain or structure very frequently.
· Depends on aggressive bypasses or highly specific tricks.
· Is useful but not suitable as a stable recommendation.
· Support cost would be too high for the core catalog.

Rule of thumb:

· If the source is valuable but makes the maintainer suffer, it probably belongs in the cursed category.

---

14. Appendix D – Recommended Workflow (Anime)

1. Execute Phase 0 (audit).
2. Synthesize results into inventory and problem map.
3. Draft and approve Phase 1 standard.
4. Apply Phase 2 to decide core vs cursed.
5. Document in Phase 3 and establish governance in Phase 4.
6. Automate health checks in Phase 5.
7. Consolidate and clean up in Phase 6.
8. Archive and close the cycle in Phase 7.

---

15. Global Success Criteria

The plan is considered successful if:

· A user can understand which anime repo to use.
· It's quick to see which anime extensions are broken and which are stable.
· A new person can contribute without guessing hidden rules.
· Experimental/cursed anime sources are clearly separated from core.
· Over time, the ecosystem improves more in order and clarity than just in quantity.

---

16. Alignment with Community Rules (Reminder)

This plan operates within the server's rules. Key alignments:

Rule How the plan complies
1. Respect All contributions and discussions follow respectful communication.
2. No Personal Attacks Issues and PRs focus on code and content, not individuals.
3. Privacy No personal information is collected or shared in this process.
4. No Spam Issues are unique and relevant; no repetitive messages.
5. Support Channels User support remains in designated channels; this is a development document.
6. No Source Recommendations This document is for internal maintenance, not user-facing recommendations. It does not endorse third-party repos.
7. No Repeated Fix Requests Known issues are tracked once; repeated requests are discouraged and handled via the issue tracker.

---

Define how cursed manga extensions in the ecosystem should be structured, documented, and maintained.

13. Appendix C – Decision on "Cursed" (Reminder)

An extension is considered cursed when:

· Requires exceptional maintenance due to extreme fragility.
· Changes domain or structure very frequently.
· Depends on aggressive bypasses or highly specific tricks.
· Is useful but not suitable as a stable recommendation.
· Support cost would be too high for the core catalog.

Rule of thumb:

· If the source is valuable but makes the maintainer suffer, it belongs here.
